characters.name: In General
characters.description: A group of children and close friends from Hawkins, Indiana. Styling themselves after their heroes in their Dungeons & Dragons campaign, The Party works closely together to defend and save each other from supernatural threats in Hawkins following the disappearance of Will Byers and the appearance of the mysterious psychic Eleven. An Adventurer Is You: Mike is the leader, Will is caught up in other dimensions, Dustin geeks out on exotic knowledge, Lucas has his "Wrist Rocket," and Eleven has actual psychic abilities.Mike:I'm our Paladin, Will's our Cleric, Dustin's our Bard, Lucas is our Ranger, and El's our Mage. Arc Words: "Friends don't lie" and variations. Ascended Fanboy: Played straight, as the four boys of the group areDungeons and Dragonsfanatics who end up in their own fantasy-like adventure. And it alsoworks to their advantage. Badass Crew: They may be kids, but they're creative, intelligent, and brave youngsters with one of them having powerful psychic abilities.

characters.name: Mike Wheeler
characters.description: The Leaderof the Party. A preteen boy who tasks himself and his friends to find their missing friend Will with the help of the mysterious young girl known as "Eleven". Act of True Love:Mike jumps off a cliff into the quarry because Troy made a genuine, timely threat of mutilating Dustin otherwise.He intervenes when Dr. Brenner and his goons come to take Eleven back, stepping into the line of fire to stop them. Mike jumps off a cliff into the quarry because Troy made a genuine, timely threat of mutilating Dustin otherwise. He intervenes when Dr. Brenner and his goons come to take Eleven back, stepping into the line of fire to stop them. Anguished Declaration of Love: After a year of not saying it outright to Eleven, Mike finally declares his love for her while she's under Vecna's curse to give her a fighting chance against her archenemy.

characters.name: Dustin Henderson
characters.description: Mike's classmate and close friend. An enthusiastic, chubby boy with a lisp who aids him in the search for Will, acting as the voice of reason. '80s Hair: After taking hair styling advice from Steve prior to the Snow Ball, he shapes his naturally curly hair into a towering mullet. He retains said mullet until the finale. Affectionate Nickname:"Dusty" from his mother."Dusty-bun" from his girlfriend Suzie, which doubles as anEmbarrassing Nickname. "Dusty" from his mother. "Dusty-bun" from his girlfriend Suzie, which doubles as anEmbarrassing Nickname.

characters.name: Lucas Sinclair
characters.description: Mike's childhood friend, next-door neighbor, and classmate, who is apprehensive about the prospect of collaboratingwithEleven in the search for Will. '80s Hair: He has a short but very distinct fade when he starts high school as an attempt to fit in with the more popular kids. By Season 4, it's grown to a spectacular late-80s flattop. Agent Scully: To contrast Dustin, Lucas tends to show the most doubt and is the most distrusting of Eleven and her powers. Badass Adorable: Is willing to strap himself up like a soldier, climb trees, and scout out a government facility if it means a chance at saving his friend. All while not being old enough to drive. Badasses Wear Bandanas: Lucas is a very action-oriented member of The Party, and dons a camo bandanna whenever things start getting dangerous.

characters.name: Eleven
characters.description: A mysterious young girl with psychokinetic powers found by Mike and his friends the day after Will's disappearance. As the series goes on, Eleven's backstory is gradually brought to light. Her original name was Jane Ives and she was acquired by Hawkins Laboratory as part of their research into superhumans. Through numerous encounters with the Upside Down, Eleven finds herself regaining what was denied to her from the start; family, friends and love. '80s Hair: By Season 3, her hair has grown out to a chin-length curly bob (a laMolly Ringwald) which she wears with either a side parting or held up with colorful scrunchies. In Season 4, she also sports longer hair with heavy bangs,until it is shaved off. Action Girl: Thanks to her psychic powers, Eleven is able to fight off attackers by either moving objects into their path, breaking their bones with telekinesis, or evenmelting their brainswith her mind. Her personal kill count is well into double figures. Season 5 has her running physical gauntlets under Hopper and Joyce's supervision so she can be physically adept as well. Actually Pretty Funny: When she and Max use El's abilities to spy on their ex-boyfriends after their temporary breakup, she catches Mike and Lucas right before they engage in aburp-and-fart contest. El immediately tears her blindfold off, looks at Max with a horrified expression on her face... and bursts out laughing. Allegorical Character: While she has plenty of character outside of that, she's also a symbol for childhood: emerging in the world as almost a blank slate in season 1 before gaining friendships, having a relationship, and slowly growing up over the seasons until she finally admits she's "not a kid anymore" in season 5.Her loss marks the end of childhood for the Party, and it's left ambiguous if she is truly dead or still out there but permanently beyond their reach.

characters.name: Erica Sinclair
characters.description: Lucas' snarky and sharp-witted younger sister. Initially a minor character, she joins the main cast starting in Season 3. '80s Hair: From hair buns, to multi braids with colorful hair decorations, to a high ponytail, and afro puffs, her hairstyles run the gamut of young Black preteen girls in the 1980s. Action Survivor: An average preteen girl who is introduced to the world of Cold War espionage, mooks out to kill her and her friends, and supernatural monsters, yet uses knowledge accumulated before those incidents and her powers of observation to survive. Later graduates to something near anAction Girlwhen she's able to take down one of Jason's basketball teammates with those same powers of observation. The moment he lets his guard down, she clocks him with a Maglite. Advertised Extra: In Season 4. While in Season 3 she joins the adventure in episode 3 out of 8, in Season 4 she joins in episode 7 out of 9, with either extremely minor appearances or none at all in the prior episodes that season. All Girls Like Ponies: She's a fan ofMy Little Pony. Dustin uses this trait as evidence for her "nerd" status, pointing out that many of the staples of the franchise (magic, dragons,The Power of Friendship) are also prominent fantasy tropes of geek culture.

characters.name: Nikki Baxter
characters.description: A new student in Hawkins Middle School in early 1985, whose mother is filling in for Mr. Clarke as science teacher while he's taking a sabbatical. Bully Hunter: Her introduction has her savings Will from getting beat up by a mean girl's boyfriend. Delinquent Hair: She's recognizable by her purple mohawk. Friendless Background: Due to the Baxters traveling and relocating frequently, Nikki never gets the chance to make any close friends and has resigned herself to all her friendships being flash-in-the-pan experiences which won't last. Gadgeteer Genius: Nikki enjoys taking random objects ans kitbashing them into something new. Two of her projects include a rocket launcher made from a microwave and climbing gloves made from ski gloves with chewing gum. The peak of her skills comes in the final two episodes of the first season, when she manages to builda homemadeenergycannonto fight the mutant Queen with, all in the span of a single day.

characters.name: Joyce Byers
characters.description: A divorced supermarket cashier and Will and Jonathan's single mother. Extremely protective of her family, she goes through immense lengths to find her missing son. '70s Hair:invokedWord of Godhas it that Joyce's hair in Season 1 was inspired by Meryl Streep's hair inSilkwood, which focused on the shag do'd whistleblower Karen Silkwood and her 1974 murder. As the series goes on, her hair gets longer and more well-kept. '80s Hair: Her hair in Season 3, while still low-maintenance is fuller and has heavier bangs. Action Survivor: Joyce willingly goes into the Upside-Down with Hopper to find her son. That's damned courageous for anyone, let alone a middle-aged mother with no self-defense training.She later even travels to Kamchatka with Murray to save Hop, and, with help from Murray and an unwitting Yuri, manages to break into Russia's nastiest prison and save him. Almighty Mom:As Vecna is left dying after being impaled on a spike by Eleven, she approaches the monster who has been tormenting her son since the first season, pulls out an axe and tells him that he "fucked with the wrong family", before hacking at his neck until his head comes clean off.

characters.name: Jim Hopper
characters.description: The town of Hawkins's Police Chief and main investigator of Will's disappearance. A divorced former law enforcer in an undisclosed big city, whose daughter died of cancer. He struggles with alcoholism and substance abuse to cope with his losses. Abusive Parents: As revealed inStranger Things: The First Shadow, Hopper's father, James Hopper Sr., was physically abusive to him, specifically punching him in the face and giving him a black eye after he tries to convince him thatVictor Creel was behind the spate of pet murders happening in Hawkins. Action Dad: After adopting El, as he's a badass Police Chief. Acrofatic: Due to his lengthy depression and not properly taking care of himself, whilst still muscular, Hopper has developed a noticeable gut. However, he shows on several occasions that he’s still impressively quick and spry for a man of his size. Notably, even in Season 3, after putting on a lot of weight, he’s still capable and fast enough to match blows withGrigori. Addiction Displacement: Hopper’s noticeable weight gain in Season 3 is implied to be the result of his having to largely give up drinking (so that he could properly look after El) and instead turning to eating more candy and unhealthy foods.

characters.name: Bob Newby
characters.description: Joyce's boyfriend at the start of Season 2 and head of Hawkins' Radio Shack. Skilled with his way around electronics and is a nice fellow overall, especially to the Byerses. Action Survivor: He's not a fighter like Jim, but still risks his life to open the research lab's doors.This trope is sadlydeconstructedimmediately afterwards; thanks to his nerves and inexperience, Bob makes a couple of mistakes such as leaving his gun behind and knocking over a broom that get him killed by a pack of Demodogs. Actor Allusion: A few toSean Astin's role inThe Goonies, which was one of the key inspirations forStranger Things.When shown the map of the tunnels, he asks, "What's at the 'X'? Pirate treasure?"He confides in Joyce that "I used to be sick all the time." His character inThe Goonieswas asthmatic. When shown the map of the tunnels, he asks, "What's at the 'X'? Pirate treasure?" He confides in Joyce that "I used to be sick all the time." His character inThe Goonieswas asthmatic.

characters.name: Murray Bauman
characters.description: An Illinois-based former journalist turned private detective, Murray initially was hired by Barb Holland's parents to locate their missing daughter and bring her home. He becomes a close acquaintance of the cast after providing critical assistance in their investigations. '70s Hair: Aside from his receding hairline, he has the facial hair, sideburns, and unruliness associated with the 60s and 70s counterculture. All There in the Manual: Although not elaborated upon in the series, actor Brett Gelman revealed in theBeyond Stranger Things 2aftershow that Murray's journalism career and family were destroyed as a result of his efforts to expose what happened in Hawkins in the aftermath of Season 1. Ambiguously Jewish: An abrasive,Brainy Brunette(albeit a balding one) sarcastic know-it-all with a German name common among Ashkenazim, a big beard, and a Chicago accent, who has an old anti-Nazi poster on his wall and is fluent in Russian. He's also played by a Jewish actor. Ascended Extra: Had a minor yet noteworthy role in Season 2. Season 3 places him in the main plot, but does not credit him as one of the main characters, likely due to only joining Hopper and Joyce halfway through the season. Season 4 credits him in the opening with the other main characters, and he is with Joyce for the entire season.

characters.name: Anna Baxter
characters.description: Nikki Baxter's mother. A biologist that briefly replaces Mr. Clarke as the Middle school's science teacher. Burger Fool: When her tenure as substitute teacher runs out, Anna chooses to stay in Hawkins, having talen on a waitress job at the local doner to make ends meet. Nikki mentions that their financial situation is pretty dire as a consequence. Like Mother, Unlike Daughter: While Nikki Baxter is a tomboyish punk with an interest in building gadgets, Anna is nerdy, conventionally feminine and specializes in plants. Red Herring: Dustin walks in on Anna chiding Daniel in an especially harsh manner, which leads Dustin to suspect she's not what she seems.As it turns out, Anna wasGood All Along, but Daniel isHorde Prime.

characters.name: Nancy Wheeler
characters.description: Mike and Holly's older sister and eldest child of the Wheelers. A straight-arrow highschooler who is starting to experiment with girlfriendhood and taking matters into her own hands when the Upside Down encroaches on her hometown and threatens her family and friends. '70s Hair: In Season 1, her long,Princess Curlshair is pinned in the style of the prior decade. '80s Hair: While she starts out the series with longPrincess Curls, her hair gets shorter and permed, resembling coifs likeMolly Ringwald,Jennifer Beals, andJennifer Grey. By Season 5, her hair has gotten even bigger and curlier, looking likeSigourney Weaver's hair inAlien (1979). Absence Makes the Heart Go Yonder: Jonathan's move to Lenora Hills in Season 4 puts their relationship to the test. Nancy feels there is a lack of communication between them that she hoped could have been solved if he had come to visit Hawkins during the spring break. She becomes frustrated and skeptical about her feelings for Jonathan and vice versa, suspecting that he is hiding something essential from her. And as if that was not enough, she is teaming up with Steve again, which triggers some old feelings for him, and starts to become jealous of Steve's friendship with Robin. Academic Athlete: According to "Stranger Things Worlds Turned Upside Down: The Official Behind-The-Scenes Companion", when she isn't wielding a shotgun at monsters, Nancy is a cheerleader and a player on Varsity Volleyball team in addition to being a member of the National Honor Society, French Club, Student Council, Model UN, and tutoring her peers in writing. She also volunteers at Meals On Wheels and at the Presbyterian Youth Fellowship.

characters.name: Jonathan Byers
characters.description: Joyce's older son and Will's brother. An adolescent loner who balances between his duties at school and contributing at home by working due to their father's abandonment. He is also a classmate of Nancy and Steve. Amicable Exes:With Nancy in Season 5, as the pair have a mature conversation about how their relationship has been making them miserable and they both want different things in life, yet they declare they still love each other even as they break up. Badass Bookworm: A photographer, amateur journalist, and member of the Yearbook Club, he's also as courageous as they come and doesn't letanythingcome between him and his loved ones. Badass Driver: In Season 3, when he and the Party are driving away from the avatar of the Mindflayer. Badass Normal: He's not an athletic jock like Steve or Billy, a cop like Hopper, or a psychic like Eleven, yet Jonathan probably takes more damage in fights than anyone not namedSteveand absolutelynone of it keeps him down.

characters.name: Steve Harrington
characters.description: A popular jock at Hawkins High with a crush on Nancy and some skewed priorities. Strikes up a strong bond with the rest of the gang after stepping up against the supernatural threats around the town on more than one occasion. '80s Hair: The best example in the show — it's very tall, with a single curl looping over his forehead from under his quiff. In Season 2 it gets longer and more mullet-y, and he admits he actually uses women's shampoo and hairspray to get the look, specifically designed to emulateFarrah Fawcett's feathery locks.Steve:[to Dustin]Faberge Organics. Use the shampoo and the conditioner and when your hair is damp - not wet, butdamp- you do four puffs of the Farrah Fawcett spray. Academic Athlete: According to "Stranger Things Worlds Turned Upside Down: The Official Behind-The-Scenes Companion" Steve is on Varsity Basketball, Varsity Baseball(The latter of which arguably foreshadows Steve's decision to become a coach in the series finale), Student Council, Key Club, Future Business Leaders of America, and Prom Committee. Season 4 also reveals he was Co-Captain for the Hawkins High School Swim Team, and a certified life-guard for 3 years. Action Survivor: The most pronounced example in the series sinceSteve absolutely sucks in a fistfight.Though he is effective at fighting withhis nail-spiked baseball bat, and has taken on several monsters from the Upside Down with different weapons at various points during the show. Alone Among the Couples: He's this among the older teens at the end of Season 4, since Nancy and Jonathan are still together and Robin has started a relationship with Vickie.

characters.name: Billy Hargrove
characters.description: Hawkins High School's new transfer student and Max's stepbrother. A vicious bully who often runs afoul of the main cast, partly due to his disdain for his stepsister and her association with her new friends in Hawkins. '80s Hair: Sports a fairly raggedy rocker's mullet, which contrasts Steve's perfectly coiffed, though still mulleted 'do. Billy does take care to style it when he's going out on a date. Abusive Parents: Billy's father never misses an opportunity to talk down to his son, and even hits him when Billy disobeys him. It's also revealed in Season 3 that Neil abused Billy's mom too, and as a result she ended up running away and leaving Billy with Neil. Agent Peacock: Billy is preening, and very popular with the ladies. He's also very vain, checking his hair in his car's rear-view mirror when something hits his car — but he's also a terrifying fighter. Alas, Poor Villain: Despite his nonstop bullying and abuse of Max, she collapses in hysterical tears whenhe dies.

characters.name: Robin Buckley
characters.description: Steve's coworker at Scoops Ahoy and former classmate. Although the two start off on shaky terms, they become close friends as they're forced to work together to investigate some strange goings-on at the Starcourt Mall. During this time, Robin proves herself as a valuable ally of the Party thanks to her good heart and brilliant mind. '80s Hair: Her hair, even at work, looks slightly punked up. It gets even more eighties when she wears it in a messy French Twist in the Season 3 finale. Academic Athlete: A bright young woman who mentions being on the soccer team in Season 3. A Day in the Limelight: The novelRebel Robinspotlights her backstory. Action Girl: She's more than competent in a fight, as shown by her performance fighting the Demobats alongside Eddie, Nancy, and Steve when they get pulled into the Upside Down.

characters.name: Eddie Munson
characters.description: Upperclassman of Dustin, Lucas and Mike, and a local punk who acts as the DM of Hawkins High's D&D club,Hellfire. Also the guitarist of a local garage band. '80s Hair: Eddie possesses very long hair, not unlike then-contemporary rock star JonBon Jovi. The Aggressive Drug Dealer: He's immediately labelled as such by Hawkins police, and the fact a girl he was selling drugs to was brutally murdered in his trailer does paint that image. While he does sell drugs, he knows Chrissy is just going to him because she's clearly stressed and is completely willing to walk away. All-Loving Hero: Beneath his rock and roll exterior, Eddie is a pretty nice guy that always looks out for others. It's explicitly stated that he sought out Mike, Dustin and Lucas when they entered high school to bring them into his group of friends, and while he may play the part of the aloof and unapproachable leader, it's made very clear he does it mostly for fun. When Chrissy comes to him for drugs, he takes time to make sure that it's what she really wants, doesn't try to push her on it, and tries to calm her down and cheer her up when he notices that she's troubled. Notably, when Chrissy dies in front of him, Eddie blames himself and believes that he was a coward for not doing anything despite there literally being nothing he could have done to save her.Even in his final moments, he asks Dustin to look out for the other outcasts and not make them feel so alone. Ambiguously Bi: Seems smitten with Chrissy but also appears to flirt with Steve, frequently invading his space and at one point calling him "big boy" in a suggestive tone of voice.

characters.name: Argyle
characters.description: A stoner and pizza delivery boy who becomes Jonathan's best friend and personal chauffeur in California. Aerith and Bob: More like Argyle and Jonathan. Of course, it's likely a nickname or possibly even his last name.noteWhile hardly common, Argyle is used as a surname. Afraid of Blood: Hinted at. The sight of blood unnerves him. Best Friend: To Jonathan; they hit it off pretty much immediately, and the supposed "slacker stoner" goes out of his way to give Jonathan, Will, and El rides and act as Jonathan's relationship counselor. (Actually giving fairly good advice) Cloudcuckoolander: Coupled with hisstonertendencies, to the point where Jonathan calls him "eccentric".

characters.name: Karen Wheeler
characters.description: Mike, Holly and Nancy's mother. A housewife who serves as the voice of concern for her children, though only within the confines of their home. '70s Hair: The blown out wings she sports in Season 1 are very much a holdover from the 1970s (likely around the time Mike started grade school, judging by the Farrah Fawcett-esque influence). '80s Hair: In Season 2 she sports a frosted, hair-sprayed edifice. Season 3 shows her with very teased, blown out, curled hair, even in a ponytail. Come Season 4, she sports a crispy, even more bleached-blonde 'ramen noodle' perm, complete with an Olivia Newton-John-esque sweatband. Action Survivor: After spending four seasonsLocked Out of the Loop, Karen finally comes face to face with a Demogorgon in Season 5. When it threatens her daughter,she stares it down, smashes a wine bottle and manages to stab it enough times to leave it wounded. Sadly, she ends up hospitalised in a critical state after the fact, but it's more than almost anyone, including dozens of trained, armed soldiers in the mid-season finale, is able to do. She performs better when the Demo-dogs attack the hospital and she sets a trap for them by putting an oxygen tank into a dryer and turning them all into crispy critters. Not bad despite being heavily injured. Advertised Extra: Karen is officially considered part of the main cast in the opening credits of every season except the fourth, despite never playing a major role in an episode until the fifth and final season, specifically in the second, and later sixth, episodes.

characters.name: Ted Wheeler
characters.description: The extremely laid-back and removed patriarch of the Wheeler family. Completely out of touch with the goings-on in his household, much less Hawkins. '50s Hair: Perhaps to emphasize his Reagan support, his age, and how distant his family feels around him, he wears this style to reflect how stagnant this view of the world and his priorities are in a modern world that has, more or less, moved on from a strict view of families and what it means to be an American. This is in contrast to the family he emotionally neglects who wear '70s and '80s-style hairstyles. Adults Are Useless: The most prominent example in the show. He's useless whenever the family gets into an argument, speaks in lame baseball metaphors to a son who couldn't be less interested in sports, and instantly believes everything the government cover-up team tells him. Lampshaded in this exchange from "Dig Dug", when Dustin attempts to ask him where both of his children (who have been gone fordays) are;Dustin:Son of a bitch. You're really no help at all, you know that?Ted:Hey, LANGUAGE! Big Eater: He is often more absorbed in his food than anything serious going on, whether it's his children arguing or them being in danger. Bigger Is Better in Bed: According to Karen inStranger Things: The First Shadow, his, ah... "dingleberry" is very impressive, which she hints is one of the only reasons she's with him in the first place.

characters.name: Holly Wheeler
characters.description: Youngest child of the Wheelers and Mike and Nancy's younger sister. In Season 5, she is now an elementary schooler who's been unsettling her parents due to her habit of talking with an imaginary friend. Ascended Extra: Originally not much more than aLiving Prop, Season 5 elevates her to a major characterwho's targeted by Vecna, with her even acting as the main perspective character who's trapped in his mental realm. She even gets an episode named after her, "The Vanishing of Holly Wheeler", a successor to the series premiere. The Baby of the Bunch: Holly is consistently depicted as the youngest member of the Wheeler household, often shown in high chairs, playing with toys, or being looked after by her parents. Break the Cutie: Her arc in Season 5 consists of herhaving to deal with the trauma of being captured by Vecna and trying to escape his mental realm. Cassandra Truth:Is one of the few people besides Joyce who sees the thing living in her walls, but because of her young age, when she tells her mother, she isn't believed.In Season 3, she notices the trees rustling at the Fourth of July festival due to the Monster Spider, but her parents encourage her to look at the fireworks.By Vol 2 of Season 5 she is the only other child besides Derek who hasn't been brainwashed by Vecna's manipulations and is willing to fight and try to escape, while none of the other children believe her warnings, and even attack her when she becomes defiant.

characters.name: Patty Newby
characters.description: The adopted sister of Bob Newby. An outcast at Hawkins High who ends up befriending new student Henry Creel. Adoption Angst: Throughout the play, she has a lot of angst over being adopted, getting mocked as "The Girl From Nowhere" by the likes of Walter and worrying that her biological mother must not have cared about her to give her up.When Henry reveals that Principal Newby is her biological father and stole her as a baby, she's actually relieved, as it meant her mother loved her after all. Black and Nerdy: All of her actors have been either black or mixed-heritage, and one of the things that initially draws her and Henry together is their shared love of the superhero character Captain Midnight. Blue Is Calm: Many of her outfits incorporate shades of blue into them, and she ends up being the only calming human presence in Henry's life and the only thing still connecting him to his humanity, serving as a direct contrast to theRed Is Violentmotif of The Mind Flayer, who encourages Henry to give in to his murderous urges. The Conscience: She's this for Henry throughout the events ofThe First Shadow, essentially serving as the only thing still connecting him to humanity, in contrast toBrenner and the Mind Flayer's shared role asThe Corruptor. When he thinks he's killed her, that last connection is gone and paves the way for him to becoming theOmnicidal Maniacthat is Vecna.

characters.name: Principal Newby
characters.description: The father of Bob and Patty Newby, and the principal of Hawkins High School in 1959. Dad the Veteran: Like Victor Creel, he served in WWII and the two of them bond over this shared history together. Eye Scream: His eyes are caved inby Henry when he tries to separate him and Patty, leaving him blind and insane. Fantasy-Forbidding Father: He's very strict with Patty, apparently more so than he is with Bob, forbidding her from not just seeing boys but also taking part in the school musical. Shell-Shocked Veteran: He tries to reassure Victor while he's having a PTSD induced breakdown by relating that he saw some horrific things during his service in the War too, not that it helps much.

characters.name: Barb Holland
characters.description: Nancy's best friend and reluctant voice of reason. '70s Hair: An old photo at her parent's house shows her with a face-framing Dorothy Hamill-esque pageboy. '80s Hair: Barb styles her shiny red locks into a short, wavy style of the decade. Academic Athlete: According toStranger Things Worlds Turned Upside Down: The Official Behind-The-Scenes Companion, she was noted to be playing Varsity Softball while being a Class Treasurer and public library volunteer, and a member of the Key Club, National Honor Society, Rotary Youth Exchange, and a Mathlete. Also a childhood photo has one of her wearing a ballet costume, implying she took ballet. Alone Among the Couples: At Steve's party, she's forced to fifth-wheel alongside Carol/Tommy and Steve/Nancy.

characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Holland
characters.description: '50s Hair: Mrs. Holland wears her hair in an outmoded '50s style, which complements her role as a traditional housewife. Gaslighting: The Lab does this to them — badly. The "Department of Energy's" piss-poor attempt at selling the "Barb ran off to the bus station and got on a Greyhound to wherever" story (rather than coming up with a more character-appropriate reason for her disappearance, a fake body or a Jane Doe report meeting their daughter's description, the idiots just left Barb's ultimate fate hanging), they (quite naturally) still tried digging into their daughters disappearance with Murray's help, understandably. This leads to Nancy, Steve (well, somewhat) and Jonathan to feel guilty about being unable to tell them what really happened and inadvertently joining in on contributing to this wrong narrative, especially as the Hollands were sinking their house and savings into their search. This compels the kids to move against the Lab more actively.Nice job, Brenner & Co. Good Parents: Post-disappearance, they are both willing to blow all their money to either get their child back or at least find out what happened to her. Housewife: Marsha is a classic example, as she is seen at home during the day wearing an apron, preparing the family meal. The fact that she later offers only KFC to Steve and Nancy speaks volumes about her state of mind at that point. Mama Bear: Marsha is determined to get her daughter home or find out about her, even if it means putting the house on the market.

characters.name: Claudia Henderson
characters.description: Back for the Finale: She returns to attend her son's graduation in the final episode. Bourgeois Bohemian: Implied. While she's not vocal about her political beliefs like typical examples, she does display a Mondale/Ferraro '84 sign in her front yard and lives in the same hilly, upper-middle class area of Hawkins as the Sinclairs and Wheelers who are notably more Republican.She's also audibly cheering Dustin on when he uses his valedictorian speech as a chance to say "screw conformity" and flip off the principal. '80s Hair: Sports a teased and curled style in Season 3 and it gets more volumized in Season 4. Crazy Cat Lady: Though she's since mellowed into merely being the kind of feline lover described below, she was one of these as a teenager, taking her cat Prancer to school with her and being seen as the local "freak" because of it. She's so grief-stricken by his death that she offers a $100 reward for the person who finds his murderer. Good Parents: Very sweet, close and loving with her son, dotes on her cat.

characters.name: Walter Henderson
characters.description: Dustin's father, who is out of his and his mother's lives by the time the show takes place. Jerkass: A thoroughly unpleasant young man who, at best, annoys everyone around him and, at worst, verbally bullies them, as he did with Patty and Henry. Kissing Cousins: It's brought up several times throughout the play that he apparently made out with his cousin, which he always desperately denies. Like Father, Unlike Son: He and Dustin couldn't be more different, as while his son is a brave, kind and heroic kid, Walter is a slimy bully who constantly belittles those around him and picks on those he considers different.

characters.name: Charles and Sue Sinclair
characters.description: Lucas and Erica's parents. '80s Hair: Both wear styles associated with middle-aged professionals and suburbanites in the African American community during the decade. Mrs. Sinclair in relaxedCompressed Hairand Mr. Sinclair cropping his textured hair into a conservative style. Mrs. Sinclair's hair starts to take on an appearance equal toPrincess Diana◊in Season 4. Back for the Finale: They appear to cheer on their son at his graduation in the final episode. Dad the Veteran: Mr. Sinclair had fought in theVietnam War. Deadpan Snarker: When showing the newly enrolled Henry Creel around Hawkins High duringThe First Shadow, Sue had a witty description loaded for pretty much the entire student body. Though forWalter Henderson, she simply gives a curt:Sue:Eat shit, Walter.

characters.name: Sara Hopper
characters.description: Chief Hopper's late daughter with his former wife Diane. Baldness Means Sickness: Her bald appearance in flashbacks visually reinforces that she is undergoing chemotherapy. The Cutie: One of the reasons her dad has been long unable to cope with her loss. She was a cute little button. Daddy's Girl: She was Hop's pride and joy. Death of a Child: Died very young from a sudden illness, due to her father's unprotected exposure to Agent Orange during the Vietnam War.

characters.name: Terry Ives
characters.description: Eleven's biological mother. A middle-aged catatonic woman and former subject of Dr. Brenner's experiments. Ambiguous Situation: In the first season, it's not known whether Terry went insane from the pressure of her efforts to fight the government, or the scrubs at Hawkinsdid something to herto shut her up once and for all. Season 2 confirms that Terry was subjected to brutal electroshock therapy. This, combined with the trauma of losing — and briefly finding, only to lose again — her daughter, is what fried her brain and made her theEmpty Shellwe see today. And I Must Scream: This is precisely what Terry'sMadness Mantrasummates: Terry has been seeing certain things and hearing certain words related to Jane's kidnapping on loop foryearsnow — Becky telling her to breathe as she goes into labor. The sunflowers in her hospital room where she's lied to and told Jane was stillborn. The combination on the safe she gets the gun out of to go get Jane back at any cost. The rainbow on the doorframe outside Jane's room, where she finally confirms she was always right and Jane was kidnapped. And finally, horrifically, the voltage Brenner ordered the shock therapy machine turned to when it fried her mind. Breathe. Sunflower. Three to the right, four to the left. Rainbow. Four-fifty. Breathe... Her worst memories on repeat for eternity — Becky says Terry's stuck in a dream she hopes is good, but really Terry's been subjected to a hellishFate Worse than Death. And by the time Eleven leaves, Becky knows the truth. Imagine her caring for her sister now, hearing those words and knowing what they mean. Cassandra Truth: No one believed her when she told the world that she carried a baby to term and was taken away from her. The problem lay in the fact that she tried to fight a battle against the very people that held all records of the events, with nothing but her word to show for it.Taking matters into her own hands, she broke into Hawkins Lab to find her daughter, finding her in the "R

characters.name: Becky Ives
characters.description: Terry's younger sister and main caretaker. Agent Scully: She received the brunt force of Terry's breakdown, so is not so inclined to believe her claims of a "lost child". Arbitrary Skepticism: Played with. She's aware that Terry was experimented on, but she doesn't believe in a missing child, or the whole superpowers claims. It's hard to blame her, considering how outlandish it sounds. El showing up in Season 2 and opening the door with her powers puts a pin in that. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: When Hop and Joyce visit her and Terry, it's markedly clear that Becky has had to deal with people asking names and nosing around for a long time. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: We never see Becky after Season 2, even though she's Eleven's aunt.

characters.name: Neil Hargrove
characters.description: Billy's father and Max's stepfather. Abusive Dad:Neil is both physically and verbally abusive to Billy, which goes a long way toward explaining Billy'sJerkassbehavior. This is shown more inRunaway Maxwhere he infamouslybeats Billy with a belt.He's not the greatest stepdad to Max inRunaway Maxeither, calling her a stupid little girl for trying to help Billy, as well as trying to take her dad's place as a father, regardless of how Max feels about him, or her real father. It's made more clear when he abandons Max to leave Hawkins without a second thought. He's not the greatest stepdad to Max inRunaway Maxeither, calling her a stupid little girl for trying to help Billy, as well as trying to take her dad's place as a father, regardless of how Max feels about him, or her real father. It's made more clear when he abandons Max to leave Hawkins without a second thought. Crazy Jealous Guy: Max implies that he didn't like the amount of time that she was spending with her biological father, which is what was the catalyst of the Hargroves moving from California. He was also abusive to his first wife because he suspected (with no discernible proof that the audience sees) that she was cheating on him.

characters.name: Susan Hargrove
characters.description: Max's mother and Billy's stepmother. Adults Are Useless: She's hardly around enough to see how much of an asshole her stepson is to her daughter. Alcoholic Parent:After Neil abandons her and Max, she turns to alcohol to cope with her newfound poverty. Broken Bird: Season 4 shows she has become a stressed, emotional wreck while working two jobs to afford the trailer she and Max now live in afterNeil abandons them. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She doesn't appear in Season 5. We never see her reaction toMax waking up, or to her being in a coma in the first place.

characters.name: Suzie Bingham
characters.description: Dustin's Mormon-raised genius girlfriend from Utah whom he met at Science Camp. Affectionate Nickname: "Suzie-poo", courtesy of Dustin. Chekhov's Gunman: Introduced in name only at beginning of Season 3. Confirmed not only as real by the end of Season 3, but also the only character who knows the numerical code — Planck's constant — needed to save the world. Child Prodigy: Dustin's claims about her being a genius turn out to be 100% correct; in fact she is probably the smartest pre-adult character in the entire cast. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Despite Dustin seeing Suzie as the love of his life in Seasons 3 and 4, she's nowhere to be seen, nor is she even mentioned at any point in Season 5. Galen Matarazzo mentioned in an interview that Dustin'sincreasing cynicism and pushing everyone awaybetween Seasons 4 and 5 led to him and Suzie breaking up.

characters.name: Eden Bingham
characters.description: Suzie's older sister, who would really like her to help with their vast, unruly bunch of younger siblings. Badly Battered Babysitter: Mostly because her younger siblings are borderline crazy, their father (parents?) is virtually absent, and Suzie can barely be bothered with such mundanities. Goth: She has the look, although much closer to the "listens to The Cure" than to the "wears period Victorian lace" end of the scale. Not so much gloomy as very much put upon. Ironic Name: The not-very-religious Eden is named after the biblical Garden of Eden, which is lampshaded by Argyle when she introduces herself. Promotion to Parent: To her great dismay, she has to watch the children and divide chores between her siblings while their father wiles away in his office.

characters.name: Alexei
characters.description: A Soviet scientist working on the Gate. Chummy Commies: Provided you don't treat him as harshly as Hopper did, he's pretty friendly even with people from an enemy nation. Dying Alone:He succumbs to his bullet wound after Murray leaves him to get help. Everyone Can See It: He seems to have been under the assumption thatHopper and Joycewere already romantically and sexually involved and thinks it's hilarious that they aren't. Foil: To Steve. Steve is an American pretty-boy with little in the way of book smarts, while Alexei is a Russian scientist and isn't cool in a conventional sense. Both are captured by authority figures from enemy nations and interrogated, with contrasting results; Steve genuinely knows nothing, is understandably panicked during the whole ordeal and gets beaten and drugged despite his innocence, meanwhile Alexei does know what the Soviets are up to, stands his ground upon being questioned and ultimately manages to collaborate with his captors. Both also have an affiliation with ice; Steve sells ice-cream and Alexei enjoys slurpies.

characters.name: Enzo
characters.description: A prison guard at the Gulag holding Hopper in Season 4, which also doubles as the training ground for the Soviet Demogorgon. All There in the Manual: He's not been referred to as "Dmitri" in the show yet, but is billed as such in casting information. Chummy Commies: Corrupt as he may be, he's quite personable. It's likewise implied that he was one of the more decent guards at the prison, even before he befriended Hopper. Dirty Cop: Prison Guard, but engages in corrupt and criminal behavior, such as working with a smuggler and taking bribes from prisoners. In this case it's a heroic example, as the regime he works for is a cruel and evil one, and his "corruption" is in aiding a hero, albeit primarily for his own benefit. Dramatic Guncock: To make Yuri cooperate with their escape plan, Dmitri cocks his gun to emphasize his threat to deliver aBoom, Headshot!if he refuses to fly them out of the USSR.

characters.name: Yuri
characters.description: A Russian smuggler who profits off of the Cold War, and is hired to help get Hopper home. Actually, I Am Him: When he first meets with Joyce and Murray, he gives a spiel about the Yuri they are looking for was killed by polar bears shortly before they arrived. It isn't particularly convincing, and he is quick to assure themheis Yuri, alive and well. Affably Evil: He's a genuinely upbeat and cheery criminal smuggler who happily sells out Hopper, Enzo, and Joyce while pocketing the money they paid him. Enzo mentions that Yuri was once a far more impressive figure before his reputation sank to "peanut butter smuggler". Annoying Laugh: Yuri frequently lets out an incredibly fake-sounding laugh while he's trolling Joyce and Murray, much to their frustration. The Atoner: After all the crap he put Hopper, Joyce, Murray and Enzo through, he manages to redeem himself by tracking down a helicopter and getting them out of the gulag.

characters.name: Powell
characters.description: Chief Hopper's second-in-command in the investigation. A laid-back police officer largely uninterested in the investigation of Will’s disappearance. Big "SHUT UP!": He interrupts a mass argument between the Sinclair, Wheeler, and Henderson families with one of these. Character Development: While not much, it's noticeable. Powell started off in the beginning of the show as very disinterested and usually just following along with whatever Hopper was doing. FollowingHopper's "death" however, he is ranked up to the Chief of Police, and begins to take the job more seriously. While he's still a bit clueless, hedoestry, far far more compared to his Season 1/Season 2 self. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn't appear in Season 5, and his reaction to Hopper being alive and later reclaiming his spot as Chief is never explored. Clueless Deputy: Played with. What makes him clueless isn't so much a lack of intelligence, but rather the fact that he is too skeptical and uninterested to pick up on all the weird stuff happening in Hawkins. Hopper also seems to consider him the more reliable of his deputies. Given the competition, though...

characters.name: Callahan
characters.description: One of Chief Hopper's officers with a tendency of speaking without thinking. Character Development: While notas muchas Powell, Callahan seems to have become a bit more respectful and does put more effort in his job than in Seasons 1 and 2. Keyword beingeffort. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn't appear in Season 5. Clueless Deputy: A more straight example than Powell. Compared to him, Callahan is very obviously none too bright. Ironic Name: His last name translates to "bright-headed". Not very fitting for the rather dull Officer Callahan.

characters.name: Florence
characters.description: Hawkins Police station's secretary and clerk. A grandmotherly figure. '50s Hair: Wears a fuzzy and soft version of the style worn by HM Queen Elizabeth II. Apron Matron: She is the stern yet loving glue that holds the police department together. Her no-nonsense attitude appears to be the only thing protecting Hopper from himself at the start of the series. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn't appear past Season 3. Cool Old Lady: She is completely unfazed by her co-workers' quirks, can snark back and forth with Hopper like a pro, and shows some admiration towards Jonathan for standing up for Nancy.

characters.name: Principal Higgins
characters.description: The principal of Hawkins High School. Dean Bitterman: After Dustin pulls his valedictorian speech stunt, he threatens all the graduating seniors with summer school. Hated by All: To the point where everyone (with the exception of Chance, and Andy) at the graduation claps after Dustin flips him off. Jerkass to One: To Eddie, to the point where he blames him for causing a fight with Tommy Hagan, when in reality it's the other way around. Unseen No More: Spends most of the series asThe Ghostbefore finally appearing onscreen in the series finale.

characters.name: Tommy Hagan
characters.description: Steve's former best friend and Carol's boyfriend. A guy with an extremely caustic personality. Ambiguously Bi: Chester Rushing stated he played Tommy as having romantic feelings for Steve, in addition to being in a relationship with his girlfriend Carol. Birds of a Feather: His relationship with utter bitch Carol is a match made in heaven/hell — take your pick. The Bully: It comes with being aJerk Jock. With the exception of his equally horrible girlfriend, Tommy picks on just about everyone. Demoted to Extra: For the majority of Season 2, although in the fourth episode, his taking the time to mock Steve about Jonathan and Nancy's relationshipresults in Steve going to her house to try to win her over, running into Dustin, and ultimately becoming a member of the main cast. Needless to say, Tommy is still the same jerk in this season. By the events of Season 3, he is completely out of the main character's lives (not that anyone misses him).

characters.name: Jason Carver
characters.description: The captain of the Hawkins High basketball team and Chrissy's boyfriend. Affably Evil: A perfect mix of this andFaux Affably Evildepending on when the mood calls for it. Jason stands up for his teammates to rough play at the basketball games, shows genuine concern for Lucas at his hangover when the latter is sick and does truly care for others. However, he has just enough charisma to manipulate people and act kindly in order to bring them to his side, with examples including him "not pressuring Lucas" to join their search for Eddie, his rabble-rousing speech at the town hall, or his politely threatening scene with Nancy in the gun store. Alas, Poor Villain: With everything the guy suffered,including losingtwopeople close to him to Vecna (one of whom was his girlfriend while the other was his best friend), having to witness the second one be murdered right in front of him before carrying his body to the shore, and his genuinely misguided beliefs (although with inexcusable actions), it's difficult not to feelsomepity at his death, to say nothing of the utterly horrifying manner in which it happens.Even Caleb McLaughlin feels sorry for him.Caleb:His girlfriend died, he thought Eddie killed her, and then he was just trying to be the superhero butended up getting cut in half, sadly. Anti-Villain: While he leads the basketball team in a manhunt for Eddie so they can kill him, he's got an understandable motive in that his girlfriend was murdered and Eddie is the prime suspect. Chrissy did die horribly in Eddie's trailer, and Jason doesn't know about any of the evidence that shows it wasn't possible for Eddie to have done it. Although his pre-existing dislike and prejudice is clearly a factor in why he latches onto Eddie so strongly, and he ignores any evidence he's presented with that doesn't line up with his beliefs. In his mind, though, he is genuinelyThe Herotrying to rid their town of a violent and unstable cult-leading lunatic,unaware that he's just a minor antagonist

characters.name: PatrickMcKinney
characters.description: A member of the Hawkins High basketball team and part of Jason's witch hunt gang for Eddie. Abusive Parents: Hinted at. Lucas feels guilty for not asking where Patrick's black eye came from, and the voice Patrick hears during a vision from Vecna calls him "an embarrassment to this family." Body Horror: Dies in a similar manner as Chrissy and Fred. Character Death: He's the third of Vecna's teenage victims, after Vecna fails to kill Max. Dark and Troubled Past: While his past isn't as elaborated on like Chrissy or Fred's, Lucas's story about his black eye and the fact that Vecna targeted him hints at this. It being implied his father regularly abuses and beats him.

characters.name: Andy Harper
characters.description: A douchebag jock who follows Jason during the manhunt against Eddie Munson. Bad People Abuse Animals: He does not take Dustin putting a snake in his locker well, killing it and then using its blood todeface Eddie's grave. Big Dumb Bully: Andy fits the stereotype to a tee; he is thuggish, simple-minded, and his only reaction to situations is threats and physical violence. The Bully: Andy has taken up the role in Season 5, with him harassing Dustin over still wearing his Hellfire Club shirt to the point of forcibly ripping it whilst he's wearing it. Following Dustin getting his own back by humiliating him with a snake, Andy leads the school basketball team to ambush and viciously beat Dustin atEddie's gravefor honoring him. Bully Brutality: He and the other basketball players give Dustin a brutal beatdown in Season 5.

characters.name: Chance
characters.description: Another jock in the basketball team. Actually Pretty Funny: He smiles at the jokes that Mike and Lucas throw at Andy, such as when Lucas reminds him that his sister kicked him in the balls, making Andy give him aDeath Glare. The Dragon: To Andy, at least after he becomes theDragon AscendantafterJason's death. Flat Character: He’s not given any further characterization besides being yet another one of Hawkins’Jerk Jockswho enjoys picking on other students seeminglyFor the Evulz. His only notable scenes are when he teases Patrick and when he’s seen by Andy’s side in season five. Hate Sink: He's just as despicable as Andy.

characters.name: Chrissy Cunningham
characters.description: The captain of the cheerleading team at Hawkins High. Abusive Parents: Her mother is implied to be verbally, emotionally and physically abusive to Chrissy, body-shaming her daughter to the point she develops an eating disorder. When under Vecna's spell, Chrissy is seen to be trapped inside a nightmare version of her family home, with her mother upstairs at a sewing machine, frantically letting out Chrissy's cheerleader uniform and ranting about her being "fat". It's implied that her father was much kinder, though her Vecna-nightmare version of him has his eyes and mouth sewn shut, implying that either he was unaware of the abuse, or was but didn't do anything about it, whether for his own reasons orhis wife telling him to butt out. All Guys Want Cheerleaders: Is known as "The Queen of Hawkins High" according to Eddie, who admits he’s intrigued (and flattered) that she wants to spend time with him, even if it’s primarily to score drugs. Additionally, her boyfriend, Jason, is crazy about her, and makes sure to tell her he loves her in his speech to the school at a pep rally. Alliterative Name:ChrissyCunningham. Apologizes a Lot: Downplayed. When Eddie tells her they've met before, Chrissy apologizes to him only twice for failing to remember him.

characters.name: Fred Benson
characters.description: A member of Hawkins High newspaper. Body Horror:Fred's death is shown in even greater detail than Chrissy's. His limbs break and twist in unnatural ways, his face is disfigured into a horrific gape and his eyes are crushed in their sockets before he drops to the ground in a mangled mess. Dark and Troubled Past: He was involved in a car crash at some point, one that left him with a nasty facial scar and took the life of another teen.Vecna uses this incident to torment him before brutally murdering him. Developing Doomed Characters: Starts out as a one-dimensional bit character,but before his death we get to know him as a sassy fellow with his own thoughts, as well as having a tragic background. Dying Alone:Is the only one of Vecna's victims whose death has no witnesses.

characters.name: Vickie Dunne
characters.description: Robin's bandmate who she has a crush on. 11th-Hour Ranger:Once she gets filled in on the Upside Down in Season 5, she quickly joins up with the group for the final episodes. Ambiguously Bi: In Season 4, she has a boyfriend, but is also heavily implied to return Robin's feelings. Steve also brings up the fact that she returnedFast Times at Ridgemont Highat "that scene" (Phoebe Cates's character removes her bikini top to show off her boobs in a sexual fantasy), which leads him to believe she likes ladies. The first episode of Season 5 fully confirms her bisexuality. Birds of a Feather: It's clear why she and Robin hit it off, seeing as they're bothkindheartedband girls with a nervous streak whotalk a lot. Candy Striper: She works as a candy striper at Hawkins Memorial Hospital in Season 5. Abrief look at her IDestablishes that she has been doing so since 1984.

characters.name: Corroded Coffin
characters.description: The other members of the Hellfire Club, as well as Eddie's bandmates. Berserk Button: Canceling/postponing D&D (at least on short notice). Black and Nerdy: Jeff is a D&D-playing metalhead and the only black Hellfire-member apart from Lucas. Curb-Stomp Battle: They're on the receiving end of one when Jason comes to ask for Eddie's whereabouts and they won't tell him anything. Though they try to put up a fight they're quickly overpowered. Geek Physique: The unnamed member, "Freak #1" is of the obese variety.

characters.name: Carol Perkins
characters.description: Tommy's girlfriend. An equally caustic girl with a chip on her shoulder. '70s Hair: Her hairstyle retains the face-framing, blown out curls of the prior decade in the first season. '80s Hair: She updates her hairstyle with more bouffant waves and heavy bangs in Season 2. Alpha Bitch: Played with. She's a clear-cut example of a catty popular girl who torments those she sees as inferior, but normally seems to hang out in a group of friends entirely consisting of guys (aside from herself). Birds of a Feather: She's basically a gender-flipped version of her boyfriend Tommy. It's a horrible thing to see in action.

characters.name: Tammy Thompson
characters.description: A classmate of Steve and Robin who the latter had a huge crush on. Alliterative Name:TammyThompson. Closet Key: Tammy was the first girl Robin fell in love with. The First Cut Is the Deepest: Tammy being oblivious to Robin's feelings thanks in part to her own crush on Steve, who at the time was a massiveJerk Jockwho didn't evennoticeTammy, left Robin heartbroken and embittered until she became friends with Steve and realized she didn't need Tammy to reciprocate her feelings to be comfortable with her sexuality. High Hopes, Zero Talent: According to Steve, she wanted to move to Nashville and become a singer. Unfortunately for Tammy, her singing voice leaves a lot to be desired.

characters.name: Scott Clarke
characters.description: The boys' science teacher. A friendly, knowledgeable man and enthusiastic teacher. 11th-Hour Ranger:In the final episodes of the series, he joins up with the group officially at the same time as Vickie and Kali. Affectionate Nickname: His girlfriend Marissa calls him "Snookums". After hearing this, Murray starts calling him that as well, apparently to wind him up, though it doesn't seem to faze him. The Bus Came Back: Returns in Season 5 to teach Erica's class.He later joins up with the group full time. Cool Teacher: He's a smart, compassionate man who loves his job and acts as a mentor to the AV Club. He even purchases a ham radio for our kid heroes to play around with during lunch. Mr. Clarke is also familiar withDungeons & Dragons, which serves as a plot point, explains parallel dimensions to the boys, and tries to console them at Will's funeral. He even tells them how to build a sensory deprivation tank at night while on a date! Season 3 reveals that he has an absolutelymassivecustom built and painted D&D board in his basement. He's also one of the few peopleEricaspeaks highly of and never sasses back to.

characters.name: Troy Walsh
characters.description: The boys' classmate and school bully. A cruel, mocking kid. Ax-Crazy: Not at first, but when El humiliates him in front of the whole school, he becomesmurderouslyangry. The Bully: An initial antagonist to the quartet who likes to spend his free time disparaging Will for his homosexuality, Mike for being a "frog face", Dustin for being toothless and Lucas for being black. Bully Brutality: He threatens to cut out Dustin's teeth at knifepoint to force Mike to jump into a gorge. Even his best friend James is apprehensive about him taking it too far. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Troy is absent from the remainder of the series, save for the tie-in comicThe Bully, which reveals what he and James were up to during Season 2, and ends with him being forced to move away from Hawkins after his dad loses his job.

characters.name: James Dante
characters.description: The boys' other school bully. Mainly tags along with Troy. The Bully: He is Troy's stooge and bullies the heroes alongside him. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Like Troy, no explanation is given for his absence in the remainder of the show. The Dragon: He's a tall, heavy-set kid and serves as second-in-command to his best friend, Troy. Even Bullies Have Standards: He may be a bully and a serious jerk, but even he's disturbed by some of Troy's actions. The tie-in comicThe Bullyshows some of his softer side.

characters.name: Stacey Albright
characters.description: AnAlpha Bitchwho has a couple of encounters with Dustin, Eleven, and Max. '80s Hair: Has very crimped and frizzled red hair that she teases to high heaven, often not as aesthetically pleasing to the taste of contemporary audiences, but on-point for the time period. A Lighter Shade of Black: To all the other bullies in the series. While rejecting Dustin at the Snow Ball isneedlessly cruel, she never goes out of her way to bully others the way Angela, Tommy and Carol do, let alone be as murderous as the worst bullies that are Troy, Billy, Two and Andy. She even mellows out at the end. Alpha Bitch: Openly sneers at other kids, including Dustin and Eleven, for tripping on heels. Bitch Alert: Even before she cruelly rejects Dustin and he's had a chance to ask her, she makes derisive looks and talking trash about the Snow Ball.

characters.name: Tina Turnbow
characters.description: The Turnbows' oldest child and Erica's former friend. Alpha Bitch: Shows multiple shades of this as Erica's snooty former friend who broke off their friendship for petty reasons and has acted incredibly nasty to her ever since. Alliterative Name: Both her first and last names start with the letter T. Evil Former Friend: Downplayed. Evil is pushing it, but she was formerly a very close friend of Erica’s. However, it's revealed she broke off their friendship over an extremely petty and unfair reason, and Erica and Lucas’s comments imply she has become incredibly nasty to her since then. False Friend: She initially seems willing to forgive Erica when she turns up to seeming apologies, but it doesn’t take long for her to start accusing Erica of sabotaging her, by tricking her into eating the pie and getting her fat.

characters.name: Jeff Nelson
characters.description: The local bully during theTales From '85series. Suspiciously Similar Substitute: Jeff fills in for both Troy Walsh and Billy Hargrove as the more mundane villain the protagonists have to deal with on top of supernatural threats and amoral researchers.

characters.name: Rosario Guillen
characters.description: A classmate of the HIC that regularly butts heads with Dustin. Bespectacled Cutie: Her thick glasses make her look endearing despite her snippy temperament. Foil: She looks similar to Dustin's future girlfriend Suzie Bingham, only she's more like hisSitcom Arch-Nemesis. Token Minority: The only Latina among the recurring cast.

characters.name: Miss Harris
characters.description: Holly and Derek's homeroom teacher. Cool Teacher: A friendly woman who's doing her best to take care of her students. Unfortunately, she'sLocked Out of the Loopand doesn't realize how serious of a situation her class is really in. Gaslighting: She tells her students that the military are the good guys despite them having taken the children from their parents in the middle of the night with no warning or seemingly any protest from the parents. Reasonable Authority Figure: When Holly Wheeler beginsengaging in conversations with Mr. Whatsit, she appears more concerned than annoyed and calls her mother, Karen to express those concerns. She also makes sure to comfort her students when the military starts rounding them up and taking them to the MAC-Z zone. What Happened to the Mouse?: It's never shown what became of her after Vecna and the Demogorgons' attack on the MAC-Z, though she presumably made it out alright.

characters.name: Derek Turnbow
characters.description: A bratty, spoiled classmate of Holly Wheeler who has someseriousattitude issues for a kid his age. Acrofatic: He's pretty swift for such a hefty kid, able to turn away from Robin and Erica blocking the only exit from the barn, reach and climb up a ladder before them, then push the ladder away while the (much taller) Robin is only halfway up. Before that, he gives Will a pretty solid chase before Will manages to tackle him. Annoying Younger Sibling: Annoys the hell out of his older sister Tina. Attention Whore: The poster child for bullies and brats who are primarily motivated by attention seeking, rather than sadism. He lives to get a rise out of others. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other:With his classmates. He bullies them, they call him "Dipshit Derek"; but when he realizes "Mr. Whatsit" is trying to hurt them, he puts his own life on the line to help them. He still enjoys hitting them with a ruler, though.With his family as well. As bratty and insensitive as he is (such as when he laughs when his father falls unconscious),Henry manages to get him to break by threatening to brutally murder his entire family, and it's made clear later this threat is what keeps him in line.

characters.name: Mary
characters.description: A friend and classmate of Holly who is targeted by Vecna. Brainwashed and Crazy: When she's introduced, she seems to be a normal, friendly girl. Then she's kidnapped by Vecna and falls for his brainwashing, and it's not long before she's chanting to bring Holly "Back to the light!" and trying to strangle her former friend. False Friend: Mary is seemingly mild-mannered and slightly nerdy-looking, but when Holly defies Mr. Whatsit’s orders, Mary reveals a surprisingly hostile side to her character, turning against Holly and looking downrightscaryas she attempts to strangle her with her own necklace. Jerkass Realization: When El, Kali, and Max trick Henry into revealing the truth about his plans, Mary realizes Holly was telling the truth all along and apologizes. Mauve Shirt: One of the more notable kids taken by Henry, if only because she's Holly's best friend and has more screen presence than the rest.

characters.name: Debbie Miller
characters.description: A classmate of Holly Wheeler who is targeted by Vecna. Break the Cutie: When the military starts rounding up her and every one of her classmates, adorably earnest Debbie breaks down crying.

characters.name: Thomas Hall
characters.description: A classmate of Holly Wheeler who is targeted by Vecna. Jerkass: He’s a foulmouthed jerk who calls Holly a bitch during the seventh episode of Season 5. Of course, it should be noted that he was under Vecna's influence at the time and he quits being a problem once Vecna's exposed.

characters.name: Joshua Gunn
characters.description: A classmate of Holly Wheeler who is targeted by Vecna. Oblivious to Love: Doesn't notice that Holly Wheeler has a crush on him.

characters.name: Ashley Klein
characters.description: A classmate of Holly Wheeler. The Stool Pigeon: When she notices fellow classmate Joshua Gunn slipping out to the washroom and trying to escape through a hole leading to the tunnels, she tells the military. This is noticed by Derek, who calls her a snitch.

characters.name: Other Classmates
characters.description: Mauve Shirt: Heavily downplayed, as he's mostly as much of aSatellite Characteras the others, but Glenn is one of the three kids who gets captured by the military at the MAC-Z alongside Mary and Derek, and his name is actually spoken in dialogue. No Full Name Given: Valeria, Rebecca and Wendy's surnames are never mentioned. Satellite Character: None of the kids have much developed personality, and upon being taken to Camazotz, are almost constantly seen together.

characters.name: Larry Kline
characters.description: The corrupt mayor of Hawkins who sold out the town to communist Russians. Asshole Victim: At the end of Season 3, Mayor Kline is arrested by the U.S government after it's revealed to the public that he knowingly and willingly assistedSoviet spies with infiltrating the U.S and performing subterfugewhile they were in there. Given how much of a rancid asshole he was though, it's unlikely too many people are going to miss him. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Pretends to be a caring,Nice Guymayor but is really a slimy,JerkassSleazy Politician. Bullying a Dragon: Practically his hobby. He seems to really like mouthing off to and belittling people that are much bigger and stronger than him. He usually gets his ass beaten for it. Butt-Monkey: Guy can't catch a break, receiving beatdowns from the likes of Hopper, Joyce, and Grigori. It's actually very tricky to find one of his scenes thatdoesn'tinvolve him getting his ass handed to him.

characters.name: Winnie Kline
characters.description: Mayor Kline's wife and one of Karen's pool-going friends who is unaware of her husband's affair and shady dealings. '80s Hair: Has teased blonde hair that poofs up above her tennis visor and headband, with long flowing curls underneath. Age-Gap Romance: Larry Kline is a middle-aged mayor while Winnie is younger (her actress is only a bit older than Dacre Montgomery, who plays Billy). Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Despite his sleaziness, she is shocked and concerned when she finds Larry tied up to their bed looking bloody and bruised. Eating the Eye Candy: She shows up to the community pool to check out Billy with several other mothers (including Karen) and even serves as the lookout for when it's time to pose as Billy walks by. She also catches Steve's eye during the Jazzercise scene.

characters.name: Tom Holloway
characters.description: Heather's father and the Editor-in-Chief at theHawkins Post. Asshole Victim: A dismissive misogynist who gets brutally knocked out and taken to the Mind Flayer byhis own daughter. Then while under the Mind Flayer's control,he gets killed by Jonathan. Body Horror:He and Bruce are melted and then merge into a horrific chimera. Brainwashed and Crazy: As this is the Mind Flayer's MO, it's to be expected. Da Editor: The bombastic editor of theHawkins Post.

characters.name: Janet Holloway
characters.description: Wife of Tom Holloway and mother of Heather. '80s Hair: Sports a full "she-mullet", a style which actually emerged a little later in the decade. Bound and Gagged: The state in which she and her husband are taken to the Mind Flayer after Billy and Heatherdrug them. Happy Marriage Charade: Implied at the one dinner we see between her and her husband, where he seems very critical of her drinking and even voices stern disapproval (like it wasn't uncommon). Yet they look fantastic in photos.... Housewife: Presents the appearance of being a perfect and cheery homemaker.

characters.name: Heather Holloway
characters.description: Billy's fellow lifeguard at the Hawkins Community Pool. '80s Hair: A teased side ponytail with a scrunchie. Alliterative Name:HeatherHolloway. Bound and Gagged: Once flayed himself, Billy transports Heather to the abandoned steel mill to "join" the Mind Flayer's flesh proxy army. Brainwashed and Crazy: She gets possessed by the Mind Flayer, thanks to Billy.

characters.name: Danny Harrington
characters.description: Steve's father, who was in high school the same time as Joyce. Big Man on Campus: Swaggering down the corridor with his arm around a pretty girl, blowing off and insulting Joyce's play and even wearing a Letterman jacket, he ticks all the boxes. '50s Hair: Just like his son, his hair is done up in a popular style of the time, in his case an Elvis-esque pompadour. Jerkass: Steve describes him as a "Grade-A asshole", and while that might just be Steve's resentment, there's multiple indications that he's right. For one, the reason that Steve's mom has to go with him on business trips is that she fears he'll cheat on her without supervision, something he's apparently done before. When his high school self is briefly shown, it's to be a jerk to Joyce for no real reason. Like Father, Unlike Son: Like his son Steve, he was aBig Man on CampusJerk Jockwho got around with the ladies, bullied a member of the Byers family, andhad great hair.Unlikehis son, he had noHidden Depthsthat eventually lead into him becoming a much better person.

characters.name: Wayne Munson
characters.description: Eddie's uncle and guardian, with whom he lives. Bruiser with a Soft Center: He presents as a typically gruff, emotionally-cool working class male, yet while he's shown to be very distant when it comes to other people, he's helpful to Nancy when she asks him questions and doesn't believe Eddie to be responsible for Chrissy's murder. And although they're never shown on-screen together, it's made clear he loves his nephew and that the two of them are very close.He breaks down intoManly Tearsupon learning of Eddie's death at the end of Season 4, having never given up searching for him. Cassandra Truth: While he isn'tcompletelyright, he's the only one who believes there's a connection betweenthe Creel murders and Vecna's victims in 1986.Pretty much everyone dismisses it. Cigarette of Anxiety: Introduced smoking one, shaken up by finding a dead body in his trailer. Establishing Character Moment: Introduced sitting by himself, not talking to any of the gathered neighbors or the police, showing that he's just as much of an outsider as his nephew.

characters.name: Alan Munson
characters.description: Eddie's father and Wayne's brother, who went to Hawkins High the same time as Henry Creel. Corruption of a Minor: Eddie says while other kids were fishing and playing baseball, Alan was teaching him how to hotwire cars. Dark Is Not Evil: He has deep black hair and all of his clothes are black with the odd splash of white, and he's Hopper's initial prime suspect for the pet murders. Ultimately though, he turns out to just be a harmless drama kid. Disappeared Dad: To Eddie, due to being in jail by the time the series starts. Not that he was a good parent when he was around. Large Ham: His style of acting is very,veryhammy, and he seems unable to go a line without shouting. It's easy to see where his son got his flair for dramatic storytelling from.

characters.name: Victor Creel
characters.description: A man who was accused of brutally murdering his entire family and cutting out their eyes back in 1950s Hawkins. Was confined to a mental asylum after being found insane. Broken Bird: A proud husband and father with a mansion in 1959, now a disturbed mental patient who gouged out his eyes in 1986. Casting Gag: Robert Englund is famous for his portrayal of Freddy Krueger inA Nightmare on Elm Street, a franchise that heavily influenced Season 4's story. His character isthe father of Vecna, who's very much anExpyof Freddy. Celebrity Paradox: TheNightmare on Elm Streetfilms, which starred Robert Englund, still exist in this universe. Dad the Veteran: A family man, and saw combat during WWII.

characters.name: Virginia Creel
characters.description: Victor Creel's wife, said to have been murdered by him. '50s Hair: Sports a perky and stylish flip-do. Ambiguous Situation:Henry saysbothhis parents did terrible things. While we know about Victor's war crimes, it's not revealed what Virginia did. When he kills her, his reasoning was only that she wanted to have him committed. InStranger Things: The First Shadow, she does slap Henry when he talks back to her, and was also the one to first tell Dr. Brenner about Henry's powers. Happily Married: She and Victor were very close and depended on one another, with Victor recalling her as "my darling". He Knows Too Much:Is killed by Henry after she finds out about his misanthropic behavior and plans to have him sent to therapy for it.

characters.name: Alice Creel
characters.description: Victor Creel's daughter, said to have been murdered by him. Children Are Innocent: A carefree little girl who is excited to move into a new house in Hawkins. Death of a Child: Her age is no deterrent for the "demon",who's actually her own brother. Older Than They Look: She looks and acts like a young preteen girl, rather than a teen girl of the era, but the newspapers covering her family tragedy note she was 15 when she died. True Blue Femininity: A perfectly feminine 1950s girl who wears a blue plaid two-piece suit and hat when her family moves into Hawkins.

characters.name: Ken Turnbow
characters.description: The patriarch of the Turnbow Family and a rich property developer. The Alcoholic: It's implied he has a habit of drinking too much, with his wife complaining about it and Derek mockingly declaring “Dad’s wasted again” when the drugs in Erica’s pie kick in. Bumbling Dad: Ken seems friendly, but he’s clearly not got much control over his family. Henpecked Husband: Implied. His wife has no issues with sharply chastising him in public, with him noticeably squirming each time she does so. Informed Flaw: Lucas's comments imply that Ken is just as bad as the rest of his family. However, onscreen Ken overall comes across as the most friendly and likeable of the Turnbow's, regularly complimenting Erica on her pie and making civil conversation. Lacking his wife's condescending and snide nature, his daughter's pettiness or his son's obnoxiousness. At worst, he comes across as a bit clueless, weak-willed and likes to drink too much.

characters.name: Mrs. Turnbow
characters.description: The Matriarch of the Turnbow family. Blonde Republican Sex Kitten: Fits the stereotype of being noticeably more attractive and glamorous than her dowdy husband, as well as being quite wealthy. She likewise encourages her children to slam the door in their face of any Democrats who come to their home. Mother's Little Helpers: Derek casually admits that his mother regularly takes Valium. No Name Given: Unlike the rest of her family, her first name is never revealed. She’s even simply credited as “Mrs. Turnbow.” Parental Neglect: A little more engaged than her husband, but not by much. She apparently takes Valium or does meditations to mentally escape her family, and at least part of why Derek is such a brat is because she doesn't bother to set or enforce boundaries or to give him disciplineorencouragement.

characters.name: Bruce Lowe
characters.description: A journalist for theHawkins Post. Asshole Victim:Did anyone really cry when he got Flayed? Didn't think so. Body Horror:He and Tom are melted and then merged into a freakish chimera. Brainwashed and Crazy:He is eventually possessed by the Mind Flayer alongside Tom. Needless to say, his already creepy and assholish demeanor is amplified under its influence. Hate Sink: He's even more sexist and obnoxious towards Nancy than Tom, and unlike him, Bruce doesn't have a daughter or a loved one to redeem him.

characters.name: Cosmo
characters.description: The boss at the Weekly Watcher. Celebrity Paradox: He's voiced by Robert Englund, who actually had an onscreen role in the original series as (the older and imprisoned) Victor Creel. Creel's claims that a "demon" killed his family and not him were actually covered by the Weekly Watcher, which means Cosmo presumably signed off on a story about another character played by Englund like himself. Additionally, a standee ofFreddy Kruegercan be seen in the Baxter family's garage int he same series. Everyone Has Standards: Cosmo knows exactly what the Weekly Watcher is, but he doesn't like to rehash the same stories over and over since he knows it isn't interesting for their buyers, even if he thinks they're a bunch of idiots. Mean Boss: Downplayed. He throws out a potential story about the "sewer serpent" and calls it boring right in front of the writer who first wrote a story about the same subject, but he clarifies that it's only because he wants something new. Outside of that, Cosmo seems to actually enjoy his job.

characters.name: Charlie Dandridge
characters.description: Jeff Nelson's friend, who regularly gets targeted by each season's monsters. Fire-Forged Friends: Charlie starts out as another bully that picks on Dustin, but after being repeatedly saved by the HIC he learns to treat Dustin more respectfully.

characters.name: William Dandridge
characters.description: A miner from the founding days of Hawkins. He's known by the townsfolk as "Bloodaxe Bill" for supposedly goijg on a killing spree.
