Hero with Bad Publicity:William never killed any miners. In fact, he was tryibg to protect his miners from Samuel Hawkins, who killed him and tarnished his name out of spite. Red Herring:The Lich was initially assumed to be the ghost of Bloodaxe Bill, but in reality was another product of the Upside Down.

characters.name: Ernie Dandridge
characters.description: Red Shirt: He's onscreen for all of one scene before getting attacked by the Lich.

characters.name: Arthur Dandridge
characters.description: Charlie's grandfather. Cassandra Truth: He vandalises library records for hiding the truth regarding the connection between Samuel Hawkins and Bloodaxe Bill.

characters.name: Benny Hammond
characters.description: The towering owner of a diner and a friend of Chief Hopper. He is the first resident of Hawkins that encounters Eleven. Boom, Headshot!: His unfortunate fate at the hands of Connie Frazier. Gentle Giant: He's a hulking man whose height is even more emphasized by Eleven being such a young girl. However, once he recognizes that Eleven isn't a thief but a distressed child, he doesn't hesitate to give her food and a fresh shirt to wear. He Knows Too Much: Merely interacting with Eleven is his death sentence. It's Personal: Elevensquishes Connie Frazier's brains the next time they meetbecause of Benny's assassination.

characters.name: Marissa
characters.description: The librarian at the Hawkins Public Library. She is an ex-girlfriend of Jim Hopper. Cute Bookworm: A pretty woman who works at the Hawkins library. Official Couple: Season 5 reveals she's now in a relationship with Mr. Clarke.

characters.name: Keith
characters.description: An employee at The Palace Arcade and later, Family Video. He is a friend of Robin. Abhorrent Admirer: For Nancy, telling the boys he will give them the information they need about Max in the first episode of Season 2 if they can set up a date with her for him. Mike ishorrifiedat the prospect. Ambiguous Situation: When Steve applies for a job at Family Video, Keith initially refuses to hire him, and tells Robin (who's speaking on Steve's behalf) that Steve's "a douchebag of the highest order." Robin admits to Keith that Steve was a prick to them in high school, but it's unclear whether or not Steve specifically bullied them, or Keith just knows Steve because of his previous reputation. He is eventually persuaded to hire Steve though, and judging by how Steve manages to stay at his job for nearly 6 months, it's possible that Keith either warmed up to Steve, that Steve was good at his job, or he appreciates Steve's ability to draw the ladies into the store. Hormone-Addled Teenager: He tries to get Mike to set him up with Nancy, and hires the clearly underqualified Steve purely because Steve's status as aChick Magnetwill draw hot women into the store. Jerkass: Comes across as a smug know-it-all who has to be bribed with pretty girls.

characters.name: Doris Driscoll
characters.description: An old woman who calls the Hawkins Post after rats eat her fertilizer. Alliterative Name:DorisDriscoll. Brainwashed and Crazy: After the Mind Flayer possesses her, she is found having eatenfertilizer. Christianity Is Catholic: When Nancy is looking at photographic evidence she has found of the Mind Flayer's victims, she includes a local Catholic church's bulletin about a senior Bingo night where Doris was in attendance. Also has an Irish last name. Conspiracy Theorist: Supposedly, according to one of the misogynists at the Hawkins Post, she believed that President Kennedy was assassinated through orders of Lyndon Johnson.

characters.name: Todd
characters.description: Owner of the car commandeered by Hopper. Atrocious Alias: "The Toddfather". It's based on his first name, but after his one scene, we never learn his last name. Cool Car: A 1984 Cadillac Eldorado Biarritz convertible. Informed Attribute: He is credited as "Rich Douchebag Todd", which implies him to be aJerkass. However, in the actual show, he never does anything of that caliber; his entire screen time is just him filling up gas for his car, wondering why the heck Hopper and company are hopping into his car, falling for Hopper's ruse of Alexei being a child murderer, standing in utter disbelief as his stolen vehicle speeds away, and later talking to some police officers about said issue. Metalhead: When Hop steals his car and turns on the radio, heavy metal starts blaring out.

characters.name: Martin Brenner
characters.description: The mysterious lead researcher and owner of the Hawkins' "Department of Energy" research facility, responsible for overseeing a number of top-secret government projects to weaponize supernatural phenomena. Abusive Dad: To Eleven; he's not her real father, just a father figure, but is abusive all the same. He submits her toTraining from Hell, torture, confinement and traumatic punishments.Season 4 shows that he's a parental figure towards many other children his goons had captured on his behalf, but when the children break rules that he has put in place, he shows no qualms about torturing them as punishment. Admiring the Abomination:He reacts in awe the first time Eleven discovers the Demogorgon. He reacts similarly when he sees it firsthand, seconds before it lunges at him. He has this same reaction inThe First Shadowuponseeing the silhouette of a Demogorgon through a gateway opened by Henry. Even after it swipes a claw at him, he's more angry at the other lab staff for shutting down the experiment than anything else.He has a similar response when Eleven kills two orderlies with her powers. He reacts in awe the first time Eleven discovers the Demogorgon. He reacts similarly when he sees it firsthand, seconds before it lunges at him. He has this same reaction inThe First Shadowuponseeing the silhouette of a Demogorgon through a gateway opened by Henry. Even after it swipes a claw at him, he's more angry at the other lab staff for shutting down the experiment than anything else. He has a similar response when Eleven kills two orderlies with her powers.

characters.name: Sam Owens
characters.description: The new head of Hawkins's "Department of Energy" research facility. Seems much less sinister in his goals and approach compared to his predecessor, Dr. Brenner. Ain't Too Proud to Beg:When Sullivan finally catches up to him, he pleads for him not to kill Eleven. He even offers a compromise where he puts Eleven under to wait and see if the Hawkin's killings continue without her, but the Colonel doesn't listen and tells a sharpshooter to gun her down anyway. Ambiguously Evil: At first, it's hard to tell how noble Owens is when he forces Hopper, Jonathan, and Nancy to keep the truth while acting affable to Will.The ambiguity is reduced when we see he's quite noble, being the only person in the facility that cares about Will's well-being, and he even stays back to guide Bob, Hopper, Joyce, Will, and Mike to safety. Big Fun: Downplayed. Owens isn’t outright obese, but he is somewhat on the heavier side, and is a jovial, warm, paternal figure. It's highlighted in Season 4when compared to thetaller and skinnier, as well as much more ruthless and callous Doctor Brenner. Big Good: Or at least, he is the closest thing the series has to one. He is leading the effort to stop the Upside Down, organized Will's rescue and helps Eleven and her allies by covering up the incidents at Hawkins for their safety, arranges Eleven's adoption and her relocation with the Byers, and works to give Eleven her powers back to fight the Upside Down in Season 4.

characters.name: Connie Frazier
characters.description: A mysterious woman and a crony of Dr. Brenner. Assumes various false identities on the show. Asshole Victim: After seeing what she's willing to do in the name of government secrecy,her death at El's powers isverysatisfying. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: First appears in the guise of being a kind social worker, and looks the part. But the moment Benny's guard is down, she remorselessly shoots him dead. Cruel and Unusual Death:El kills Connie, along with a dozen other government agents, by telekinetically scrambling their brains inside their skulls, causing blood to leak from their eyes. One might presume that if Connie hadn't murdered Benny in cold blood right in front of El, her fate would have been more humane. Dark Action Girl: Seemingly the only female member of the government agency, who carries out the murder of Benny in Episode 1.

characters.name: Ellen Stinson
characters.description: An agent serving under Owens in Season 4. '50s Hair: Wears her dark hair up in a old-fashioned "roll" updo, likely a holdover from when she first started working as an agent. Good Counterpart: The loyal middle aged field operative right hand woman of a scientist formerly in charge of Hawkins Lab — she's as good as Connie Frazer was evil. Lady in a Power Suit: She's introduced via a slow upward pan, revealing killer heels as she steps out of her patrol car, and she sports a boxy and professional suit with broad shoulders at all times, befitting the era and her profession. The Lancer: Has a professional and friendly relationship with Owens and actively does his bidding.

characters.name: Agent Harmon
characters.description: An agent serving under Owens. A subordinate of Stinson and Wallace's partner. Badass in a Nice Suit: He wears a typicalMen in Blacksuit and saves the kids during a gunfight with some soldiers. Doomed Hurt Guy:He's wounded in one episode and dies in the next a few hours after fleeing the fight that wounded him. One-Man Army: He's a middle-aged dude with a beer gut, a double-chin, and only a handgun for protection. To top it off, his partner is immediately incapacitated at the start of the firefight. But Harmon keeps calm and methodically guns down several heavily armed soldiers while shepherding the boys to safety. Underestimating Badassery: Initially, he appears to be a lazy agent who's just there to babysit Mike, Jonathan, and Will while watching TV. However, when Colonel Sullivan's men show up to the house with the intention of killing everyone there, he manages to put up an impressive fight against the soldiers while getting the teenagers to safety. It's primarily because of his actions that Mike, Will, and Jonathan are able to escape and survive.

characters.name: Agent Wallace
characters.description: One of the agents serving under Owens along with Harmon. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: Pleads with Sullivan not to kill Eleven when the Colonel's torture finally breaks him and he reveals her location. Agonizing Stomach Wound: He is shot in the stomach by one of Sullivan's soldiers, which takes him out of commission for the entire firefight in the Byers's house. Made of Iron: Initially, he seems somewhat ineffective when he is shot right away by Sullivan's men, but he proves to be able to withstand their attempts to torture him for an impressively long time. Uncertain Doom: It is unknown if he was allowed to live after giving up Eleven’s location or if he waskilled after.

characters.name: Shepard
characters.description: A scientist who made an ill-fated journey into the Upside Down. Cruel and Unusual Death: When the Demogorgon finishes with him, all that's left is a bloody scrap of clothing. Sacrificial Lamb: Shepherd appears solely to show the dangers of exploring the Upside Down even when the searcher has official equipment.

characters.name: Elevator Scientist
characters.description: One of Brenner's assistants. Bald of Evil: He isn'ttooevil, but he stands by while El is put in a sensory deprivation tank and the only hair on his head is on the sides of it. Death by Looking Up: He hears the Demogorgon above him and looks up in the elevator before he is dragged upwards to his death. No Name Given: He is never identified by name in any of his few scenes, and he is credited simply as "Elevator Scientist". Personal Mook: He stands in the 2 flashbacks alongside Dr. Brenner and the Senior Scientist, which means he's an assistant to one or both of them.

characters.name: Nerdy Tech
characters.description: One of the scientists serving under Owens in Season 2. Geek Physiques: He's rather heavyset and also a "nerdy" scientist. Gosh Dang It to Heck!: He reacts to the demodogs starting to break through their protective cell by muttering "Mary, mother of Joseph..." Mauve Shirt: He's given the most focus of the scientists monitoring the Upside Down in Season 2, but he still gets killed with the rest in the elevator. No Name Given: He's never named in any of his scenes, and is credited only as the "Nerdy Tech".

characters.name: Ray Carroll
characters.description: A retired orderly who was in charge of"treating"the test subjects. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He has two daughters who are hiding in their room in fear when their father is being tortured. When El realizes this, she ultimately decides not to kill him, and prevents Kali from doing so as well. Fat Bastard: He was one during his time at Hawkins Energy Lab, torturing Kali with a cattle prod. Just Following Orders: This is the excuse he uses when El and Kali confront him over his past sins. Kali coldly calls him out on it, and tells Carroll that he knew what he was doing was evil. Karma Houdini: Eleven decides to spare him and stops Kali shooting him for the sake of his children, so the most punishment he gets for his crimes at Hawkins Lab is being bashed around a bit and robbed.

characters.name: Two
characters.description: Another of Dr. Brenner's subjects, and apparently one of the most talented, who bullies Eleven in their time on the lab. Alas, Poor Villain:Although he was abullyand aHate Sink, his death is brutal and disturbing, with even Eleven being horrified by it despite all he did to her.Not to mention, like Eleven, he was kidnapped as a baby and raised in a lab, so it's kinda hard to blame him for something Brenner is responsible for. Asshole Victim:While his death is horrific, you won't find many people crying for him. He belittles, bullies, assaults and finally threatens to murder Eleven: needless to say, he had it coming. Bad Liar: AJustifiedexample, since Two lacks the social skills to lie convincingly. He still tries. Big Jerk on Campus: In this case, the "campus" is the Hawkins Laboratory, and Two pretty much sees himself as the most powerful of Brenner's subjects, and therefore the most popular out of all the kids.

characters.name: The Mind Flayer
characters.description: An enormous monster of immense power that serves as the primary will driving every living thing in the Upside Down. Achilles' Heel:In the series finale, the Mind Flayer's physical form is a gigantic spider-like kaiju that the party would have no hope of defeating on their own, but it's also bound to Vecna, who is much smaller and still mortal despite it all. Thus most of the party lay down fire on the Mind Flayer itself while Will and El use their psychic powers on Vecna, effectively doubling the damage. When Vecna is killed, the physical Mind Flayer also goes still. Aliens Are Bastards: A malevolent extradimensional entity which is attempting ahostile takeover of our realmthrough horrific means. Ambiguous Gender:Will refers to the Mind Flayer as "he", meaning it either identifies as male or this is simply how Will makes sense of its existence and connection with him. It's very likely the latter, as all the other characters (unless talking about it with Will) refer to the creature as "it", it is a hive mind of several entities and is also described as a "virus", which typically lack gender, and the Duffers have stated its true nature is impossible to comprehend.In addition, in the after-show, BeyondStranger Things, the Mind Flayer is referred to interchangeably as "he" or "it", suggesting either its gender is weirder than we understand, "he" is simply a sort of nickname, or it's up to audience interpretation.Further complicating matters is that in Season 3, the sole time we hear it speak for itself in Eleven's vision, it refers to itself with plural pronouns such as "we" and "us" after beginning its monologue by using "me and "I," singular pronouns.In the early stages of Billy's Flaying, however, Billy hallucinates Heather telling him to "Bring me tohim", twisting this into a full circle.Season 5 adds in the twist thatthe Mind Flayer and Henry Creel mentally combined on some level, implying that both the sporadic gendering as male and the plural pronouns are the res

characters.name: The Hawkins Demogorgon
characters.description: A nigh-indestructible, superficially humanoid carnivore in a relentless pursuit of any and all victims in sight. An Arm and a Leg: It appears to sever its own foot to escape being set on fire in a bear trap, although it also seems to have healed by the time it confronts the Party. Big Bad Ensemble: With Dr. Brenner in Season 1. Brenner is the one responsible for unleashing the Demogorgon and spends the entire season trying to cover it up while hunting Eleven, while the Demogorgon kidnaps Will Byers and terrorizes the town on its own accord.It completely takes over the role ofBig Badin the finale when it (seemingly) kills Brenner and becomes theFinal Boss. Bizarre Alien Senses: It can somehow sense blood from across dimensions. Conditional Powers: Is extremely attracted to the scent of blood and only attacks actively bleeding victims outside its dimension; in some cases he will transcend the barrier if he gets even the tiniest whiff of blood. One of the reasons it doesn't immediately kill Will is because he's not bleeding.

characters.name: D'Artagnan
characters.description: A small creature from the Upside Down who is adopted by Dustin, who initially confuses it for an exotic tadpole. Alas, Poor Villain:Its death is portrayed in a solemn light — in spite of it eating Dustin's cat, the creature was a loyal pet. Androcles' Lion:It allows Dustin to pass when he feeds it Three Musketeers Candy bar due to Dustin taking care of it. Body Horror: It got into our dimension bygestating inside Will's body as a parasite. Grew Beyond Their Programming:Or rather, his hive mind. While Dart still became dangerous after maturing into a Demodog, he seems to remember the kindness that Dustin showed him when he was in the boy's care and behaves like a slightly tamed wild animal when Dustin gives him another Three Musketeers bar. Being enslaved to the Mind Flayer or not, Dart (and presumably the rest of his species) does have some sense of self outside of the Mind Flayer's control, which proved useful when it remembered Dustin enough to not immediately attack him.

characters.name: The Demodogs
characters.description: The adolescent forms of the Demogorgon's species. All Animals Are Dogs: They howl like dogs at night. One of them also makes a dog-like whine in season 5. Attack Its Weak Point: Hopper and the Hawkins Energy Lab staff don't have much luck with body shots, but when Hopper is defending Eleven from them at the Gate, he's forced to shoot the first one in the face, which takes it out quickly, and he switches to headshots after that. Conservation of Ninjutsu: In the second season, the Demodogs are less formidable than the Demogorgon from the first season. A single adult demogorgon was a massive threat, but it takes an army of the adolescents to pose even close to the threat the original posed. Justified, since they are juveniles who, presumably, lack the tough hide and massive strength of a fully-grown Demogorgon. They also do collectively end up killing far more people than the one adult did, even if each juvenile goes down easier if isolated. They rarely are isolated, though. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: While not the main antagonists of Season 2, they do create a nice contrast to the Adult Demogorgon. While the adult was aNigh-InvulnerableLightning Bruisercapable of taking on entire squads of armed men without a scratch and required nothing short of complete telekinetic disintegration to kill; the Demodogs are much weaker and squishier, requiring only a few well-aimed bullets to put down. They make up the discrepancy withnumbers.

characters.name: The Soviet Demogorgon
characters.description: A demogorgon that the Soviets were able to capture. They feed it prisoners. Arc Villain: The biggest threat in the Russia storyline of Season 4. An Arm and a Leg:Hopper slices off one of its arms before finishing it off. Brought Down to Badass: This Demogorgon lacks theConditional Powersthe Hawkins Demogorgon had, but is just as deadly a physical combatant - arguably even more so. Curb-Stomp Battle: Hopper, Dmitri and several other prisoners stand together with some weapons hoping to put up a fight. Within a minute, only Hopper and Dmitri are left alive, and even that is mostly due to them exploiting its weakness to fire to just about hold it off.

characters.name: The Flayed
characters.description: People and animals infected by the Mind Flayer. Largely left to operate on their own, the Mind Flayer can "activate" them to serve its ends. And I Must Scream: The Flayed are fully aware of what they're doing under the Mind Flayer's influence and are helpless to stop it, up to and includingtheir own bodies melting down into a raw, contaminated, bloody liquid to make up the main body. Body Horror: The Mind Flayer can use its control over the Flayed to melt them into a sludge of raw materials that it can shape into monstrous forms. Extreme Omnivore: The Flayed have a craving for random things like fertilizer and cleaning fluids, ammonia appearing to be the common factor, likely to preemptively destroy their organs to give the Mind Flayer more malleable materials to work with. Face Full of Alien Wing-Wong: How they became Flayed. The proto-body of the Mind Flayer's Avatar shoved something down their throat to infect them and turn them into its slaves.

characters.name: The Hospital Monster
characters.description: A creature made from the remains of two humans after they were Flayed. Blob Monster: As a mass of liquid meat held together only by the will of the Mind Flayer, it can discorporate back into a blob to ooze under doors and through vents. Body of Bodies: The result of two Flayed(Bruce and Tom, to be precise)forming a creature independent of the Mind Flayer. Evil Is Visceral: It can be described as an arthropod with(and of)skin. Failure Gambit:As implied by Flayed!Billy, the Hospital Monster's other purpose is to test whether or not the Mind Flayer's main avatar (composed of many more bodies) is ready to take on El and the party, meaning it knew full well the Hospital Monster stood little chance against her.

characters.name: Demobats
characters.description: Airborne Mook: They are flying creatures from the Upside Down who are linked to Vecna's hive-mind. All There in the Manual:Stranger Things VRreveals that the Demobats were responsible for Billy's car crashing in Season 3, which directly led to himgetting flayed. Bat Out of Hell: Bats are the closest animal they resemble and they inhabit anEldritch Location. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They don't appear in Season 5. Fragile Speedster: They're fast enough to keep pace with a bike, but alone they aren't much of a threat, as Steve rips one apart with his bare hands (and teeth), though he was likely hopped up on adrenaline from them trying to eat him at the time. Up that number to two or three however and they can become significantly more effective.

characters.name: Vine Dog
characters.description: The first of the vine monsters. Call a Smeerp a "Rabbit": It looks more like a possum or a rat than a dog. Escaped from the Lab: The vine dog was introduced in its initial vine stage in a lab. Once it developed limbs, it broke out. Small Role, Big Impact: The vine dog never encounters the HIC and is killed off by the scientist who discovered it, but before it died the vine dog released spores that would lead to the creation of the Aboleth and Gourd Horde.

characters.name: The Aboleth
characters.description: A vine monster that formed around Charlie Dandridge. Call a Smeerp a "Rabbit": It doesn't look much like a shark once you get a good look at it. It looks more like a centipede with skin like a frog. Shark Fin of Doom: The snow shark got its initial name from its dorsal spines protruding out of the snow it was hiding under.

characters.name: Gourd Horde
characters.description: Vine monsters that bonded with pumpkins. Pumpkin Person: The pumpkins form heads while the vines form bipedal bodies. Zerg Rush: Individually they're not much stronger than a teenager, as Lucas and Max were able to overpower them mano mano, so the entire horde chases them into the nearby barn.

characters.name: Pumpkin Queen
characters.description: A more powerful variant of the Gourd Horde, which formed from a pumpkin pie that bonded to Rosario Guillen. Early-Bird Boss: The most dangerous of the vine monsters that the HIC has to contedn with before they start upgrading their weapons and tactics. King Mook: It's bigger and stronger than the Gourd Horde thanks to bonding to a human. More Teeth than the Osmond Family: The Pumpkin Queen's lips resemble the petal-like structure of the demogorgons, but with extra rows of teeth in the center.

characters.name: Mulligan Creatures
characters.description: A pair of vine monsters that spawned at the Mulligan Bros. Sawmill. Primal Stance: They walk on all fours despite having arms, due to their upper bodies being disproportionately large. Red Right Hand: One of them has a buzzsaw embedded in its forehead. Top-Heavy Guy: They've both got bulky torsos with small heads and hind legs. Wake-Up Call Boss: Just when it seems like the HIC figured out that the vine monsters can't survive without a host, the Mulligan creatures prove them wrong by attacking immediately after their own hosts were prised out of them.

characters.name: Vine Crawlers
characters.description: The fully matured forms of the vine monsters. Evil Is Visceral: They look near-identical to the Mulligan Creatures, but with a less streamlined exterior that resembles bones and musculature. Praetorian Guard: The vine crawlers are the chief minions of Hordak.

characters.name: Hordak
characters.description: The strongest of the vine monsters. Eviler than Thou: She devours Horde Prime just to get the last of the serum and empower herself enough to open the gateway to the Upside Down. Final Boss: Of the first season. My Death Is Just the Beginning: The final scene of Season 1 shows a brilliant blue flower emerging from her remains. Said flower ends up being aSequel Hookfor Season 2. Tainted Veins: Her body becomes illuminated by green veins after ingesting the last of Horde Prime's serum.

characters.name: Kali
characters.description: Another one of Dr. Brenner's test subjects, a British girl of Indian descent who became the leader of a nomadic street gang. Action Girl: Even without her powers, Kali is quite physically impressive, managing to overpower a soldier by ambushing him and stealing his gun in the confusion.She also briefly gets into a gun fight with several of Kay’s soldiers and comes very close to escaping the base all on her own. Agonizing Stomach Wound:Akers shoots her in the stomach before being killed by Eleven, butKali doesn't seem to care about the woundbefore bleeding out. Almost Dead Guy: If Mike is right about her in the finale,she was heavily wounded and on the verge of dying, but still managed to cast an illusion of Eleven from the Upside Down Lab, making everyone believe she'd died while Eleven escaped into the tunnels. Awful Truth:When she first attempted to escape from Dr. Kay’s lab, Kali ended up running through a series of hospital rooms housing multiple pregnant women who were receiving transfusions of her blood, which made her realize how deep Dr. Brenner’s experimentations ran.

characters.name: Axel
characters.description: Arbitrary Skepticism: Despite working for Kali and knowing full well about her powers, he initially refuses to believe Kali when she says Eleven is also psychic. Ax-Crazy: The most violent of the gang. Blood Knight: Seems to enjoy a good fight, particularly near the end of "The Lost Sister" during his shootout with the cops. Boom, Headshot!:He's the only one of Kali's gang we actually see die onscreen, getting his brains blown out courtesy of Dr. Kay's special forces. The Lancer: Axel often disagrees with Kali, but still shows enthusiasm to her cause (perhaps more so than the others.)

characters.name: Dottie
characters.description: The newest member of Kali's gang. Beware the Nice Ones: She supports Kali and is decently friendly to Eleven but she is a member of a somewhat dangerous group. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: She was in a mental institution until recently, and she is... off. Meaningful Name: "Dottie" is a slang term for crazy, and she was in a mental hospital until recently. Signature Headgear: Often wears a ribbon in her hair.

characters.name: Funshine
characters.description: The Big Guy: He's a huge guy who fills a door-frame and acts as the team muscle. Fluffy the Terrible: He's a rugged, intimidating gangster who serves as the gang's muscle. He's also named after aCare Bear. Gentle Giant: He is a soft-spoken, personable guy (when not on the job), open with his gratitude towards Kali and calls Eleven "Miss Jane". Scary Black Man: Deliberately invoked; he's the largest and strongest member of the gang and is used for intimidation when the gang are on the job, but is otherwise very friendly and laid back.

characters.name: Mick
characters.description: Everyone Has Standards: She told Axel not to hurt Eleven, stating that she's just a kid. Gender-Blender Name: Mick is typically a man's nickname, yet she is a woman. Getaway Driver: Serves as the gang's wheelman. The Smart Guy: She is practical and too smart to play cards with Dottie and Funshine. Also, she's generally less "wacky" than the others and acts as the team's watcher and getaway driver.

characters.name: The Nevada Spy
characters.description: A Soviet agent who stole lab equipment from the Nevada Experiment, and whose cave hideout was stumbled upon by an eight year old Henry Creel. Ambiguous Situation: At least in the show itself. Nothing about this man is properly explained in Henry's memories, such as how he obtained a chunk of the Mind Flayer in the form of a rock in a suitcase, who he is, how he busted his leg and ended up in the cave, and who he thinks is the "they" who sent Henry after him. Cruel and Unusual Death:Henry beats him up with a rock and then uses his new powers to cave in his skull after being taken over by the Mind Flayer. Small Role, Big Impact: Despite only being mentioned offhandedly by Brennerand having a brief scene in Season 5, by stealing technology from the Nevada Experiment and leaving it in his hideout, he inadvertently allowed Henry to enter Dimension X, meet the Mind Flayer, receive psychic powers and set the entire story of Stranger Things in motion. On a more minor note, his cave hideout also gave Henry such horrific PTSD that he refuses to enter the memory of it, giving Max a bastion of safety within Vecna's mind. Trigger-Happy: By the timeHenry came across him in the Nevada mineshaft, he's so terrified and exhausted after being on the run that he's prepared to shoot and kill an eight year old boy who's offering to help him. When Henry comes a little too close, he doesn't hesitate to shoot him through the hand, and scrambled to reload and finish the job, forcing Henry to beat him to death with a rock.

characters.name: Stepanov
characters.description: A Soviet General in charge of the Gate project. Bad Boss: Season 3beginswith a number of techs being vaporized by the device used to open a gate. Stepanov registers no interest or concern about it, beyond executing the head scientist for failure and warning his replacement that he has one year to succeed before he suffers the same fate. Bald of Evil: A murderous, bald-headed officer behind some unethical experiments. Greater-Scope Villain: While ultimately being the mastermind behind the Russians' actions in Season 3 he only appears briefly in the first episode, withGrigoricarrying the weight throughout the season.AsThe Stingershows, the destruction of the Hawkins Gate ultimately did little to disrupt his plans. Karma Houdini:Alongside the rest of the Russians he somehow manages to evacuate from Hawkins before he can be apprehended by the military.

characters.name: Ozerov
characters.description: A Soviet Colonel overseeing the Gate project in the field in the US. Actually Pretty Funny: When his interrogation of Steve achieves little outside of making Steve try to bribe him with ice-cream, Ozerov cracks up. All There in the Script: His name is never mentioned in the show proper, being only known from promotional materials. Karma Houdini:Alongside the rest of the Russians he somehow manages to evacuate from Hawkins before he can be apprehended by the military. Orcus on His Throne: He's not a particularly active villain and only has a handful of scenes as an interrogator.

characters.name: Grigori
characters.description: The leader of a group of Soviet assassins. All There in the Script: His name is only given in the subtitles/transcript. Arc Villain: He's the most prominent villain of the Soviet plotline in Season 3, as their enforcer assigned to kill Hopper and Joyce when the pair get too close to their operation. Badass Biker: His main mode of getting around in Hawkins is with his motorcycle and is extremely formidable. Notably this detail is what tips Hopper off to Mayor Klein's involvement with him. Badass Normal:Given whom he's based on, it should come as no surprise that he's incredibly dangerous, regardless of what his bones are made of.

characters.name: Melnikov
characters.description: The warden of theKamchatkaprison, within which Hopper finds himself locked up in Season 4. All There in the Script: His name is never spoken in the show itself. He's only ever named in the credits. Arc Villain: For Hopper and Joyce's storyline in Season 4. He has no connection to the Vecna conflict at all, save for the revelation he's been experimenting with the Upside Down and he has a gate of his own. Asshole Victim: He's brutally mauled by the Demodogs, but considering everything he put his prisoners through, it's unlikely the viewer will shed any tears for him. Big Bad Wannabe: From his treatment of his prisoners to the experiments he runs on the creatures of the Upside Down, Melnikov seems to believe himself to be more powerful and in control than he actually is. In reality, he's small potatoes compared to Vecna and the Mind Flayer, and his experiments on the latter end upcosting him dearly.

characters.name: Oleg
characters.description: A prisoner theKamchatkaprison, within which Hopper finds himself locked up in Season 4. All There in the Script: His name is never spoken in the show itself. He's only ever named in the credits. His last name comes from his prisoner uniform. Cruel and Unusual Death: The Demogorgan throws him to the ground, swallows his entire head and eats it. Dramatic Irony: Oleg was the one who said that if they stick together, they might stand a chance at surviving. He’s the first to run when the monster kills his fellow prisoners. The only prisoners who stuck to the plan, Dmitri and Hopper, ended up surviving. Forgotten Fallen Friend: He briefly befriends Hopper and Enzo in prison, but they don’t mention him after he dies in the pit.

characters.name: Angela
characters.description: The high school's residentAlpha Bitchintroduced in Season 4. '80s Hair: She sports a high ponytail held in place with a scrunchie and heavy bangs. Alpha Bitch: The resident popular girl at El's new school who constantly bullies her over her outsider status. Asshole Victim: Whatever her yes men andWord of Godsays to the contrary, no tears are shed for this chick when El non-lethally whacks her in the face with a roller skate hard enough to put a hole at the bridge of her nose and give her a concussion, considering she's the school's residentAlpha Bitchwho terrorizes El for basically no reason. Beauty Is Bad: She's very pretty and a deeply unpleasant person.

characters.name: Jake
characters.description: Angela’s equally horrible boyfriend. Expy: While Angela is aLighter and SofterChris Hargensen fromCarrie, he seems to be the same for Billy Noland....again, no more friendly, but he and Angela's prank is only dumping a milkshake on Eleven instead of pig blood and he never makes an attempt tomurderEleven. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: With how much of a vile person he is, he at the very least seems to care about his girlfriend, given he was concerned about Angela when she gets hit by the roller skate. For the Evulz: Like Angela and the rest of her gang, he is most extremely immature and does not have aFreudian Excusefor it. Hate Sink: As with Angela, he has absolutelyzeroredeeming qualities and is, by far, theloosestdefinition of a human being.

characters.name: Captain Brenner
characters.description: Captain of the USS Eldridge during the Philadelphia Experiment and the father of Dr. Martin Brenner, and the first known human in the Stranger Things universe to encounter Dimension X and its denizens and live. Alien Blood: Like Henry after him, his exposure to Dimension X gave him a never before seen blood type. Like Father, Unlike Son: From the little we see of the Captain, he seems to be a decent, level-headed man who just wanted to earn a little bit more money for his family by volunteering his ship for the Philadelphia Experiment. His son, of course, is a sociopath obsessed with trying to break through to and control the Upside Down. They're implied to have a fraught relationship, since Captain Brenner mentions to one of his men that Martin told him he hated him. Sole Survivor: Of the entire crew of the USS Eldridge that took part in the Philadelphia Experiment, he is the only survivor, with the rest being slaughtered by Demogorgons who swarmed the ship when it arrived in Dimension X. The Speechless: He didn't speak a word from the moment he arrived back in our world from Dimension X, either too traumatized by what he saw there or being physically unable tountil he's possessed by the Mind Flayer to speak to Henry.

characters.name: Lt. Colonel Jack Sullivan
characters.description: An army officer who oversaw Brenner's experiments, and is charged with covering them up. When Vecna's murders start, he believes Eleven is responsible and begins a quiet man-hunt for her. Allegorical Character: Acting as a counterpart to the Hawkins lab in season one, Colonel Sullivan can be seen as the embodiment of the more negative side of the US military during the Cold War. He presents himself as a patriot who is protecting America from the threat of communism, when in reality he is a hypocritical, paranoid bully who abuses his authority to carry out unsanctioned acts, justifying them in response to threats that are no where near as dangerous as he believes or flat out only exist within his own mind and whose actions only get innocent people killed (notably US citizens), largely as collateral damage. He likewise flagrantly violates the very same laws and standards he claims to be upholding, and approaches every situation with unnecessary and overwhelming levels of violence, most of which does nothing to actually help his goals. Ambiguous Situation:It's unknown if he's aware that Dr. Kay was using Kali's blood to experiment on pregnant women and create more numbered children like Henry, Kali and Eleven, especially given he doesn't seem to know anything about the Demogorgons or Vecna or had ever encountered them before, whereas Kay knows all about the Upside Down monsters and their weakness to heat. Asshole Victim:After kidnapping God knows how many children, violating an ungodly amount of his own laws,having a civilian home shot upbecause he thinks the Byers are hiding Eleven, ordering Eleven killed by his men despite Owens' pleas, torturing a federal agent by locking him in a sweat box to cook, and possibly killing Owens, this self-righteous, hypocritical moron gets his just desserts after Vecna single-handedly curb-stomps the military forces at the Mac-Z and then blows up a gas tank with some grenades to burn them alive, with Sullivan last seen writhing on the

characters.name: Dr. Kay
characters.description: A government scientist and the overall head of the US Military stationed in Hawkins to deal with the Upside Down. Admiring the Abomination: Takes a keen interest in the ecology of the Upside Down.When Hopper is being strangled by a tentacle monster in a cage, she explains its reactions to heat and cold as though she was explaining it to a science student. All for Nothing:She's an extreme anti-communist, and wants Eleven back in the Army's custody so that she can get to Brenner's endgame of using Eleven to create more psychic children who could then be trained to undetectably assassinate high-ranking Soviets. Little does she know that, if events in this world go the same as ours, the Soviet Union is about to begin fracturing (with the republic of Estonia declaring its independence barely a year after the events of this season, on November 16, 1988) and will cease to exist barely three years after that, on December 26, 1991, meaning that ultimately, Project Nevada ends up as a meaningless waste of manpower, resources, and lives.Whilst she seemingly gets away without suffering any actual punishment, by the end of the season, this is what all Kay’s efforts amount to. All her experiments have failed, all her research was either lost or rendered worthless following El and Kali’s demise, and the destruction of Upside Down. Thus, she’s left presumably holding the bag for the entire project being one big failure. Little does she know that, if events in this world go the same as ours, the Soviet Union is about to begin fracturing (with the republic of Estonia declaring its independence barely a year after the events of this season, on November 16, 1988) and will cease to exist barely three years after that, on December 26, 1991, meaning t

characters.name: Lieutenant Robert Akers
characters.description: Colonel Sullivan's right hand man and chief enforcer. Ambiguous Situation:While he does know about the Upside Down and the secret door that houses Kali/Eight (albeit he doesn't actually know what's behind the door, referring to it as just "secret shit" that he doesn't know about when Jim interrogates him), it's unknown if he's aware that Dr. Kay has been trying to restart Brenner's experiments by infusing pregnant women with Kali's blood to create more super-powered children, especially considering his hatred for "freaks". Asshole Victim:Unlike his men, who El grants a quick death, she forces Akers to be aware for several moments of what's happening before she makes him use his pistol to shoot himself in the head. Considering he’s proven to be a murderous fanatic, no tears are shed for him and he 100% deserved it. Benevolent Boss: Whilst taking time to relieve himself, he gives his men a smoke break. He’s likewise furious at Hopper and El killing them.He later even flat-out voices his displeasure to Dr. Kay about the fact that she is still more concerned with pursuing Eleven than with the fact that so many of their men have been killed by Vecna, and the children they failed to keep safe are potentially still in danger, but she just tells him to ask his unit commander for more men. Black-and-White Insanity: Akers is revealed to subscribe to Colonel Sullivan’s view that their side is in the right and thus anyone they oppose must be in the wrong. He notably doesn’t have any guilt about being involved in the massacre of unarmed scientists, as they were supporting “a freak.”

characters.name: Sergeant Luis Ramirez
characters.description: An NCO stationed in Hawkins to help with the quarantine. All There in the Script: His name is only given in the credits. Attack the Mouth:In addition to being impaled through the eyes, he's stabbed through the head and out the mouth by Vecna's tentacles. Cruel and Unusual Death:Despite being theToken Good Teammateof the military, Ramirez receives perhaps the most brutal and graphic death of them all when he's impaled through the face by Vecna with his tentacles during hisone-sided massacreof the Mac-Z. Everyone Has Standards:He's the only one to object to Dr. Kay's plans to round up the children at the base to be used as bait, calling it reckless.

characters.name: Helicopter Pilot
characters.description: A pilot under Sullivan's command who attacks theNINAfacility. Cruel and Unusual Death: If the chopper's explosion didn't instantly blow him up, he probably burned to a crisp in the wreckage. Tough luck. Face Death with Despair: He completely freaks out when Eleven uses her powers to manipulate the helicopter and send it tumbling to the ground, hysterically screaming at the sniper that he can't control it and has no idea how to stop it before the chopper explodes. No Name Given: His name is never mentioned. Villainous Friendship: Either he or the sniper was friends with Lt. Akers.

characters.name: Helicopter Sniper
characters.description: A sniper who joins the attack on theNINAfacility. Asshole Victim: He had no qualms about shooting Eleven to death (or at least trying to), willingly participating in the attack on theNINAfacility and killing at least 9 scientists, orkilling Brenner (which hekinda deserved due to how awful of a person he was), even though he did try saving El, so tears aren't going to be shed when El sends his helicopter tumbling to the ground to kill both him and the pilot. Cold Sniper: He's a US army sniper who's pretty apathetic about shooting Eleven, theNINAlab scientists, orBrenner. He's a pretty good shot, too. Cruel and Unusual Death: He either blew up when the helicopter did or burned alive in the crash or wreckage. No Name Given: We never learn his name.

characters.name: King and Wright
characters.description: Two military officers who arrest Robin. Cruel and Unusual Death:Torn to shreds by a demodog. Jerkass: They angrily dismiss Robin's pleas for them to evacuate the hospital by telling her "we don't need to do shit" and barking at her to shut up while calling her a junkie. Oh, Crap!:They're both shocked by the sudden presence of a demodog that suddenly arrives without any warning before being mauled. Profane Last Words: One of them says "Oh, shit!" upon being ambushed by a demodogbefore they're both killed.

characters.name: Chapman
characters.description: Another military soldier. Cruel and Unusual Death:He gets his face stomped on by a Demogorgon. Heroic Sacrifice: Well, villainous (and it's not even a sacrifice), buthe shoves Sullivan aside to save him when the first demogorgon arrives, getting his face crushed into mulch for it. Red Shirt:He's given a name, but shares the same outfit as the rest of the non-Wolf Pack soldiers at the MAC-Z, receives almost no dialogue, nothing to distinguish him from the others, and is the first one to be iced during the Demogorgon attack on the base.

characters.name: Williams
characters.description: A jerkass military soldier. Hate Sink: He is a complete piece of garbage with zero redeeming qualities who shoves a kid into the military base like he's an animal and even threatens to have him blasted by the Kryptonite speakers. Jerkass: All of his screentime has him act like a complete asshole, as he angrily tells Derek that the military base is off-limits when he pulls up with his lunchbox, then threatens to have the sonar devices on the truck murder him when he thinks they're laser blasters. Uncertain Doom:It's unknown if he was killed in the fight at the MAC-Z against Vecna and the Demogorgons. What Happened to the Mouse?:He never shows up again after Derek is walked into the military base, and whether or not he was killed by Vecna and the Demogorgons in the ensuing fight is unknown.

characters.name: Lonnie Byers
characters.description: Joyce's ex-husband and Jonathan and Will's estranged father who lives in Indianapolis. A deeply selfish man and womanizer. Abusive Parent: Of the emotionally abusive variety. It's clear he's been chipping away at both his sons' egos over the years. But, has focused mainly on Will. Joyce mentions that he would call him homophobic slurs. His comment about Jonathan having gotten stronger when the latter shoves Lonnie off of him also seems to imply that he may have pushed Jonathan around when he was younger as well.noteThis is not helped by the fact that a later scene between Billy and his father (who isdefinitelya physical abuser) is shot and blocked in a very similar way. Age-Gap Romance: As revealed inThe First Shadow, he began dating Joyce when she was still in high school and he had already graduated (with the West End version stating that he's 25 while she's 18, and the Broadway version describing Joyce's interest in men who are only "18 and over"). Bait the Dog: In the fifth episode, he comes back to Hawkins for Will's funeral. It seems like he really cares and is willing to make things right with his family. Then it's revealed that he is putting on an act, because he plans to cash in off of Will's death by suing for money. Calling Parents by Their Name: Jonathan refers to him as "Lonnie".
